_meta.grounding: COSO ICF 2013 enumerates 5 components and 17 principles and stops there: it does not enumerate controls, and its nearest equivalent to a control list (the 87 points of focus) is copyrighted. So every template here is an AUTHORED ICFR baseline at testable-control grain, not a port of a published list. Codes, titles, objectives, successCriteria, testingMethodology and all task content are original to this repo. The principle codes P1-P17 and the five component names are the public enumeration and are the only COSO-derived identifiers used.
_meta.grain: One control = one owner, one frequency, one test procedure, one evidence set. A template covering several activities at once cannot express that provisioning is per-event while access review is quarterly, forces one test plan to bundle unrelated procedures, and leaves coverage unable to say how far a domain has got.
_meta.licensing: No COSO body text and no points of focus are reproduced. A legal review is advisable before customer release; see docs/implementation-notes/2026-09-20-coso-framework.md.
_meta.frameworkKeyNote: Deliberately the SAME key as src/data/libraries/coso-icf-2013.yaml, so the library import and this fixture converge on ONE Framework row. Every other framework in this repo exists twice under two keys, one per authoring path, and usecases/framework/coverage.ts records that a tenant's links hang off whichever row its database got. COSO has no such split yet and should not acquire one.

framework.name: COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework
framework.description: Five components and seventeen principles of internal control. The framework states what must be true of a system of internal control; the controls that achieve it are designed by the organization, and the templates here are this product's opinionated ICFR baseline.

requirements.title: Commitment to integrity and ethical values
requirements.summary: Standards of conduct are written down, endorsed at the top and reinforced in practice, with a route for raising concerns and evidence that departures are examined rather than absorbed.

requirements.title: Board oversight responsibility
requirements.summary: A governing body independent of management oversees the design and operation of internal control, with its remit written down and management required to account for control performance.

requirements.title: Structures, authority and responsibility
requirements.summary: Reporting lines and authority are allocated so responsibility for control is unambiguous, and the limits are enforced where the work happens rather than existing only on paper.

requirements.title: Commitment to competence
requirements.summary: The organization attracts, develops and retains people capable of performing the controls assigned to them, with competence expectations stated and development tracked.

requirements.title: Accountability enforcement
requirements.summary: Individuals are answerable for their control responsibilities through objectives, performance assessment, and reward structures examined for the pressures they create.

requirements.title: Suitable objectives specified
requirements.summary: Objectives are stated clearly enough that risks to achieving them can be identified, including what is reported, to what standard, and what level of misstatement would matter.

requirements.title: Risk identification and analysis
requirements.summary: Risks to stated objectives are identified across the organization and analysed as a basis for deciding what to do about them, with criteria applied consistently and responses approved.

requirements.title: Fraud risk assessment
requirements.summary: The potential for fraud is considered explicitly, covering misappropriation, fraudulent reporting and corruption, and must address management override of the controls it owns.

requirements.title: Significant change identification and analysis
requirements.summary: Changes that could materially affect internal control are identified and their consequences assessed, with the assessment reaching the control design rather than stopping at the change.

requirements.title: Selection and development of control activities
requirements.summary: Control activities are selected and developed to reduce identified risks to an acceptable level, with duties divided and relied-upon controls distinguished from the rest.

requirements.title: General controls over technology
requirements.summary: Where controls depend on technology the technology is governed: access granted on approval and withdrawn when due, changes authorised and tested, operations run and recovered reliably.

requirements.title: Deployment through policies and procedures
requirements.summary: Control activities are carried into practice through owned policies and procedures, with evidence that those who must follow them received them and periodic re-approval.

requirements.title: Use of relevant information
requirements.summary: Internal control depends on information that is relevant and of sufficient quality, with sources known, completeness and accuracy demonstrated, and definitions and ownership settled.

requirements.title: Internal communication
requirements.summary: Information about internal control reaches the people who act on it, including what they are responsible for and a route for reporting a control that has failed.

requirements.title: External communication
requirements.summary: The organization communicates with outside parties on matters affecting internal control, and what comes back is routed to someone and acted on rather than received and filed.

requirements.title: Ongoing and separate evaluations
requirements.summary: Internal control is evaluated through monitoring built into operations, through evaluations conducted separately from the activity examined, or both, planned against the controls relied upon.

requirements.title: Evaluation and communication of deficiencies
requirements.summary: Deficiencies are collected centrally, assessed against criteria separating a deficiency from a significant one and from a material weakness, and remediated by a named owner to a tracked date.

templates.title: In-scope processes and significant accounts documented
templates.description: The documented set of business processes behind the in-scope accounts and disclosures, each written to show where a transaction starts, the systems it crosses and the point it reaches the ledger, with the places it can go wrong marked on the flow.
templates.objective: To ensure every in-scope account and disclosure is tied to a documented process showing where its transactions start, the systems carrying them and the point they post to the ledger.
templates.successCriteria:
A process inventory covers every in-scope account and disclosure, and no scoped line is left without a process behind it.
Each document shows where a transaction starts, the systems and interfaces it crosses, and the point it posts to the ledger.
The places a transaction can be lost, duplicated, mispriced or booked to the wrong period are marked on the flow, not described in general terms.
Each document names a preparer and the business owner who confirmed it, with the date of that confirmation.
Processes hit by a system migration, outsourcing move or reorganization carry a version later than the change.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved list of in-scope accounts and disclosures - that list is the denominator for the coverage work below.
Obtain the process inventory and the current document held for each process named on it.
Collect the walkthrough notes and owner confirmations dated inside the period.
Request the period's record of finance system migrations, outsourcing moves and reorganizations.
Obtain the account-to-process mapping the inventory was built from.

Analysis:
Reconcile the approved account list to the inventory and name every in-scope line with no process behind it.
Sample eight processes weighted to the largest balances and read each document for origination, systems crossed and posting point.
Walk two transactions through each sampled process and compare what happened with what the document claims.
Compare document version dates against the period's change record to find processes that moved but were never rewritten.
Test whether the marked failure points name a condition that could actually occur rather than a generic risk word.

Output:
Coverage table of in-scope accounts against documented processes, with unmatched accounts listed.
Walkthrough findings per sampled process, separating documents that were wrong from documents merely out of date.
Schedule of processes touched by a period change whose document predates it.
List of processes carrying no confirmed business owner.

title.en: Derive the process inventory from the approved scope

description.en: Start from the scoping decision rather than from what happens to be documented already, so the inventory is a consequence of the accounts in scope instead of a survey of existing paperwork.

text.en: Take the approved in-scope account and disclosure list as the starting population.
Name the process or processes that produce each line on that list.
Split a process performed differently at two entities or locations into separate entries.
Flag scoped accounts where no process can be named, since those cannot be documented yet.
Fix the inventory at a stated date so later coverage checks have something to measure.

title.en: Document each process from origination to ledger posting

description.en: Write the flow end to end: the event that starts a transaction, the hands and systems it passes through, and the journal that lands in the general ledger, so a tester can follow it without asking.

text.en: Describe the event that starts a transaction and the record it first creates.
Name each system and interface the transaction crosses, in the order it crosses them.
Identify every handoff between teams, entities or outsourced providers along the flow.
State the journal or posting that brings the transaction into the general ledger.
Record the preparer and obtain the business owner's dated confirmation of the flow.

title.en: Mark where a transaction can be lost or misstated

description.en: Turn the narrative into something a control can be attached to by marking the specific points of failure on the flow instead of listing risk words alongside it.

text.en: Work along the flow and mark each point where a transaction could fail to be captured.
Add the points where an amount, a rate or a counterparty could be entered wrongly.
Mark the cut-off points at which a transaction could fall into the wrong period.
State the account and assertion each marked point would damage if it occurred.
Leave the marks on the flow diagram itself so later matrix rows can cite them.

title.en: Refresh a process document when its system or provider changes

description.en: Documentation goes stale the moment the process moves, and the in-period rewrite is what keeps the flow matching the transactions actually being processed.

evidenceHint.en: The re-issued document for each in-period change, showing the version date, what moved, and the owner who confirmed the new flow.

text.en: Watch for system migrations, outsourcing moves and reorganizations affecting an in-scope process.
Re-walk the affected part of the flow with the people now performing it.
Re-issue the document with a new version date and a note of what changed.
Tell the owners of any matrix row that cites a point of failure the change removed or moved.

title.en: Re-trace a sample of transactions end to end

description.en: The only test that separates a document describing the process from a document describing an intention is to pick real transactions independently and follow them through.

text.en: Select transactions from the ledger rather than from a list the process owner supplies.
Follow each one from its originating record through to the posted journal.
Note every step taken in practice that the document does not describe.
Confirm the systems named in the document are the systems the transaction actually crossed.
Return documents that diverge to their owner with a date for the rewrite.

templates.title: Risk-control matrix maintained per in-scope process
templates.description: A matrix held for each in-scope process pairing every identified misstatement risk with the controls relied on to address it, each row carrying the assertion, the control's type and frequency, its owner and the evidence it leaves behind.
templates.objective: To ensure each in-scope process holds a current matrix pairing every identified misstatement risk with the controls relied on, the assertion addressed and the evidence each control leaves.
templates.successCriteria:
Every process in the inventory holds a matrix, and every risk on it carries at least one control a named person performs.
Each row states the assertion addressed, whether the control prevents or detects, how often it runs, and whether it is manual or system-enforced.
Each row names the evidence the control leaves, specific enough for a tester to request it by name.
Risks carrying no control, and controls attached to no risk, appear on the matrix rather than being absent from it.
The version in force is later than the newest process change it is meant to cover.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the process inventory - the population of matrices expected - and the matrix held against each process on it.
Obtain the account-to-process mapping so each matrix can be tied to the balances behind it.
Collect the version history of each matrix across the period.
Request the control descriptions behind a sample of rows and the evidence each row names.
Obtain the period's process changes from the change record and reorganization notices.

Analysis:
Reconcile matrices held against processes in the inventory and name the processes with none.
Sample twenty-five rows drawn across at least six processes, weighted to the largest balances, and test each for assertion, control type, frequency, owner and named evidence.
Count rows whose risk carries no control and controls attached to no risk, expressing both as a share of the sample.
Request the named evidence for ten sampled rows and check that what arrives matches what the row promised.
Compare matrix version dates with the period's process changes to find matrices that never moved.

Output:
Coverage table of in-scope processes, matrix held, and the date of the version in force.
Attribute results row by row, showing which of the five attributes were missing.
Schedule of uncovered risks and unattached controls, with the process each sits in.
List of rows whose named evidence could not be produced on request.

title.en: Set the row attributes every matrix has to carry

description.en: Agree the column set once, centrally, so matrices written by different process owners can be read against each other and a missing attribute is visible as a blank rather than a house style.

text.en: Agree the attributes each row carries: assertion, control type, frequency, owner and evidence.
Define the permitted values for control type and frequency rather than leaving free text.
State how a row cites the point of failure it comes from in the process document.
Issue the agreed layout to every process owner expected to hold a matrix.

title.en: Pair every identified risk with a control someone performs

description.en: Work down the marked points of failure and attach the control relied on at each, leaving the unmatched ones visible instead of quietly dropping them from the matrix.

text.en: Bring each marked point of failure from the process document onto the matrix as a row.
Attach the control relied on to address it, naming the person who performs it.
State the assertion the control addresses and whether it prevents or detects.
Leave a row visible where no control exists, rather than removing the risk.
Mark controls that appear on no row, so the effort spent on them is reconsidered.

title.en: Name the evidence each control leaves behind

description.en: A control that cannot be tested is not yet a control, so each row has to say what artefact its performance produces and where a tester will find it.

text.en: State for each row the artefact the control produces when it is performed.
Say where that artefact is held and how long it is retained there.
Reject an entry that names a system rather than an artefact a tester can read.
Test one row's evidence by asking for it cold and seeing what arrives.

title.en: Revise the affected rows within the quarter a process changes

description.en: The matrix earns its place only while it matches the process in front of it, so each quarter's changes are worked into the rows they touch instead of waiting for an annual refresh.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's matrix versions, each showing the rows added, amended or retired and the process change that prompted them.

text.en: Collect the process changes, system releases and role moves landing in the quarter.
Amend, add or retire the rows each change touches, with a reason against each.
Re-point rows that cite a point of failure the change has moved or removed.
Issue the revised matrix with a version date and tell the control owners affected.

title.en: Request the named evidence for a sample of rows

description.en: Reading the matrix proves only that someone wrote it; asking for what the rows promise is what shows whether the controls described are the controls being performed.

text.en: Draw a sample of rows across several processes, weighted to the largest balances.
Ask the named owner for the evidence the row says the control leaves.
Compare what arrives with the frequency and control type the row states.
Record rows where nothing could be produced, and treat them as unsupported.
Return the findings to the process owner with a date for correction of the matrix.

templates.title: Key versus non-key control designation approved
templates.description: The decision to rely on a control as key, taken against stated criteria, reasoned on the record and approved by a named person before a testing plan is built on it or a control is left out of one.
templates.objective: To ensure a control's key or non-key standing is a reasoned decision taken against stated criteria and approved by a named person, rather than a label applied when the matrix was written.
templates.successCriteria:
Stated criteria say what makes a control key: the assertion it covers alone, the balance it protects, and whether anything else would catch the same misstatement.
Every designation carries the criterion it was judged against and a short reason, not a tick.
Each decision names its approver, the date given, and the matrix version it applies to.
A control moved from key to non-key carries the reason for the move and the control now relied on instead.
No control is tested as key, or left out of testing, ahead of the approval that places it in that class.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the designation criteria in force and the date they were approved.
Obtain the whole control population from the matrices - key and non-key together, since a test run only over the key controls has no denominator.
Collect the designation records: criterion cited, reason given, approver and date.
Obtain the period's testing plan and the controls it covers.
Request the log of controls whose designation moved during the period.

Analysis:
Reconcile designated controls to the control population and name every control carrying no decision at all.
Sample fifteen key controls across at least four processes and read the recorded reason against the criterion cited.
Sample fifteen non-key controls sitting on material accounts and test whether the criteria would have carried them into the key population.
Match the testing plan to the approved key list, identifying controls tested without a designation and controls designated key but not tested.
Re-perform the approval check on every designation that moved in the period: approver named, date present, and earlier than the first test relying on it.

Output:
Population reconciliation naming controls with no designation decision.
Findings on key designations whose stated reason does not meet the criterion cited.
List of non-key controls the criteria would have made key.
Schedule of designation movements with approver and date against each, flagging any approved after testing had begun.

title.en: Determine the criteria that make a control key

description.en: Write down what earns a control the reliance before any control is looked at, so the designation is a test applied to the population rather than an opinion formed control by control.

text.en: State the balance and assertion exposure above which a control is presumed key.
Add the criterion covering a control that addresses an assertion on its own.
Say how a redundant control behind an existing key control is to be treated.
Have the criteria approved and dated before any designation is judged against them.

title.en: Judge each control in the matrix against those criteria

description.en: Work through the whole control population rather than the obvious candidates, recording for each the criterion applied and the reason the judgement came out as it did.

text.en: Take every control row from the in-scope matrices as the population to judge.
Apply each criterion in turn and write the reason the control passed or failed it.
Name the other control relied on where a control is judged non-key for redundancy.
Mark the matrix version the judgement was made against.
Assemble the results into a single key list rather than leaving them across matrices.

title.en: Put the judged list before its approver ahead of any testing

description.en: The designation is a decision someone has to own, and the approval has to land before the testing plan is built, since a plan built on an unapproved list cannot be corrected afterwards.

evidenceHint.en: The approval record behind each decision: criterion cited, reason given, approver, and the date it was granted.

text.en: Present the judged list with its reasons to the approver named in the criteria.
Capture the approval with a date, rather than an email acknowledging receipt.
Re-present a control whose designation changes, with the reason for the change.
Hold the testing plan until the designations it depends on are approved.

title.en: Contest non-key calls sitting on material balances

description.en: The designation that costs nothing to make and everything to be wrong about is the one that takes a control out of testing, so those calls are the ones re-examined by somebody other than their author.

text.en: Select non-key calls on the accounts carrying the largest balances and the most judgement.
Re-apply the criteria independently and reach a view without reading the original reason.
Compare the two views and take the differences back to the person who judged it.
Refer unresolved differences to the approver for a decision on the record.

title.en: Match the approved key list against the testing plan

description.en: Two documents that should be the same population drift apart quietly, and the reconciliation between them is where a control tested without approval or approved without testing shows up.

text.en: Line up the approved key list against the controls the testing plan covers.
Name controls in the plan that carry no approved designation at all.
Name approved key controls that no test in the plan reaches.
Check the approval date of each designation falls before the first test relying on it.
Close the differences by amending the plan or re-presenting the designation.

templates.title: Control design effectiveness assessed for key controls
templates.description: The judgement, reached control by control from a walkthrough of a live transaction, on whether each key control as designed would prevent or detect the misstatement the matrix attaches it to, with the shortfalls logged as design deficiencies.
templates.objective: To ensure each key control is judged, from a walkthrough of a real transaction, on whether its design would prevent or detect the misstatement the matrix relies on it to address.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control on the approved key list carries a dated design conclusion, and that list is the population worked through.
Each conclusion rests on a walkthrough of at least one live transaction traced to source documents.
The conclusion states whether the control as designed would prevent or detect the misstatement it is attached to, and who reached that view.
Where the design does not hold, the shortfall is logged as a design deficiency with a severity and a named remediation owner.
A control whose design changed after its walkthrough is re-walked before the conclusion is relied on.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the approved key control list at the assessment date - its count is the denominator for coverage.
Collect the walkthrough papers: the transaction selected, documents inspected, person interviewed and the date.
Obtain the design conclusion recorded against each assessed control.
Obtain the design deficiency log with severity, owner and due date.
Request the record of key controls whose design was altered after their walkthrough.

Analysis:
Reconcile assessed controls to the approved key list and name every key control carrying no conclusion.
Sample twelve conclusions across at least four processes, weighted to controls that address an assertion alone, and read each against its walkthrough paper.
Re-perform two walkthroughs from that sample, selecting the transaction independently and tracing it to the same documents.
Test whether each adverse conclusion reached the deficiency log, and whether the severity follows a stated basis rather than the assessor's preference.
Compare walkthrough dates with the design change record to find conclusions overtaken by a later change.

Output:
Coverage of the approved key list, naming the controls left unassessed.
Re-performed walkthrough results, showing where the paper and the process diverged.
Schedule of adverse conclusions traced through to the deficiency log, with any that stopped short.
List of conclusions predating a design change to the control they cover.

title.en: Timetable a walkthrough for every control relied on as key

description.en: Plan the year's work from the approved population so coverage is a scheduling decision made in advance rather than whatever was reached before the deadline arrived.

text.en: Take the approved key list as the population and count what has to be covered.
Order the work so controls covering an assertion alone are walked first.
Book each walkthrough with the person who performs the control, not their manager.
Leave slack in the timetable for the re-walks a design change will force.

title.en: Walk a live transaction through each key control

description.en: Follow one real item through the control as it is performed, inspecting what the performer inspects, so the conclusion rests on the process rather than on its description.

text.en: Select a transaction that the control would have acted on during the period.
Sit with the performer and follow the control as it is applied to that item.
Inspect the source documents and system records the performer actually opens.
Ask what would have happened had the item been wrong in the way the risk describes.
Keep the paper: item selected, documents seen, person interviewed and date.

title.en: State the design conclusion and the basis it rests on

description.en: Reach a view for each key control on whether its design addresses the misstatement it is attached to, and say what in the walkthrough supports that view.

text.en: Write the conclusion against the risk the matrix attaches the control to.
Cite the walkthrough evidence the conclusion rests on, by document and date.
Say plainly where the control depends on another control being performed first.
Name the person reaching the conclusion and the date they reached it.

title.en: Raise a design deficiency where the walkthrough breaks

description.en: An adverse conclusion has to become something with an owner and a date, since the failure this control exists to catch is a design gap noted in a working paper and never carried anywhere.

evidenceHint.en: The log entries opened from this cycle's walkthroughs, each carrying a severity, a remediation owner and a due date.

text.en: Open an entry for each control whose design does not address its risk.
Grade the severity against the balance and assertion exposed by the gap.
Name a remediation owner and a date the amended design is due.
Tell the control's tester, so operating tests are not run against a design already known to fail.

title.en: Contrast the conclusions with the year's control failures

description.en: Where a control judged well designed then failed in operation, one of the two judgements was wrong, and the comparison is the cheapest way to find which conclusions were written optimistically.

text.en: Collect the control failures, exceptions and errors recorded across the year.
Match each back to the design conclusion written for that control.
Examine every case where a favourable conclusion preceded a failure in operation.
Decide whether the design conclusion or the operating test was at fault.
Feed the pattern into next cycle's criteria for how walkthroughs are performed.

templates.title: SoD conflict matrix defined for financial roles
templates.description: An approved statement of which duty combinations may never rest with one person across the financial processes, written as duties rather than job titles so it survives a reorganisation.
templates.objective: To ensure the duty combinations that may never rest with one person in a financial process are settled in an approved conflict matrix that enforcement and detection can both be tested against.
templates.successCriteria:
The matrix pairs duties rather than job titles, so a reorganisation that renames posts cannot silently retire a conflict.
Every in-scope cycle contributed the duties it splits, including purchase to pay, order to cash, payroll, treasury and the ledger close.
Each pair states the misstatement or loss the combination would permit and a severity fixing whether it may ever be accepted.
The version in force carries a dated approval from the officer accountable for financial reporting and visibly supersedes the previous one.
Process, system and assurance teams work from that published version, not a local copy.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the conflict matrix in force during the period, carrying its version number and approval date.
Obtain the process inventory listing the financial cycles in scope and the duties each was decomposed into.
Collect the preceding version of the matrix together with the change record between the two.
Request the distribution record showing which teams hold the current version and from what date.
Obtain the severity scheme that decides which pairs may never be accepted.

Analysis:
Reconcile the duties named in the matrix against the process inventory, and list any in-scope cycle that contributed none.
Take a sample of ten pairs and test each for a stated misstatement and a severity; a pair carrying neither can be neither enforced nor accepted on any basis.
Examine whether pairs are expressed as duties rather than as named posts or system role codes, which would rot at the next reorganisation.
Set the approval date against the period start to judge whether the version relied on was in force throughout.
Trace the differences between the two versions to the process or system change that prompted each.

Output:
Statement of the matrix version in force during the period, its approver and the date it was approved.
Schedule of in-scope cycles with the duties and pairs each contributed, naming those that contributed none.
List of pairs carrying no stated misstatement or no severity grade.
Finding on whether role design, detection and assurance are working from the approved version.

title.en: Enumerate the duties each financial cycle actually splits

description.en: Decompose every in-scope cycle into the duties a transaction passes through, so the pairs are drawn from what people do rather than from what their posts are called.

text.en: Take the in-scope cycles from the significant account and process scoping.
Break each cycle into the duties a transaction passes through, end to end.
Note for each duty the system it is performed in and the records it touches.
Write duties as acts, so a renamed post cannot retire a duty with it.
Circulate the decomposition to each process owner for correction before pairing.

title.en: Draft the forbidden pairs and the misstatement each would permit

description.en: Pair the duties that must not be held together and set against each pair the specific misstatement or misappropriation the combination would allow, with the severity that decides whether it can ever be accepted.

text.en: Pair duties whose combination lets one person both create and conceal an error.
State against each pair the misstatement or loss the combination would permit.
Grade each pair, marking those that may never be accepted on any basis.
Test the draft against an error or fraud the organization has actually seen.
Settle contested pairs between the process owner and the accountable officer.

title.en: Issue the approved version to every team that applies it

description.en: Put the approved matrix into circulation under a version number and date, so role designers, the detection rule owner and the reviewers are all working from one text.

evidenceHint.en: The distribution record for the version in force, naming each recipient team, the date it was issued, and the superseded version it replaced.

text.en: Number and date the approved matrix before it leaves the owner's hands.
Send it to role design, the detection rule owner and internal audit.
Withdraw the superseded text from the places these teams actually read.
Note who received the current version and on what date they received it.
Answer interpretation questions in writing, against the version issued.

title.en: Examine the pairs a reorganisation or system change has made stale

description.en: Test whether the matrix still describes the organization as it now is, taking the period's restructures, system replacements and new cycles and asking what each did to the duties and the pairs.

text.en: List the restructures, acquisitions and system changes the period brought.
Trace each to the duties it created, merged or moved between people.
Mark pairs whose duties no longer exist, and cycles carrying no pairs at all.
Refer the amendments required to the matrix owner with a date against each.
Conclude whether the version in force remains fit, and say so in writing.

templates.title: System role design enforces the SoD conflict matrix
templates.description: Roles and entitlements in the financial systems are built and granted so that a combination the conflict matrix forbids cannot be assembled out of what one person holds.
templates.objective: To ensure roles granted in the financial systems are built and assigned so that no person can assemble from them a combination of duties the conflict matrix forbids.
templates.successCriteria:
Every role in an in-scope system maps to the duties it grants at transaction level, not to the menu names the product shipped with.
A role that internally combines a forbidden pair is split or rebuilt before anyone is assigned to it.
The assignment path refuses, or diverts to a recorded acceptance, any grant that would complete a forbidden pair with what the user already holds.
Emergency, firefighting and support roles that can bypass the design are time-boxed and appear in the same mapping.
Each role build, change and grant in the period was checked against the matrix version in force on its date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the role catalogue of each in-scope financial system, listing every role and the transactions or objects it grants.
Obtain the mapping from role to matrix duty, with its author and the date it was last refreshed.
Draw the population of role builds, role changes and role assignments in the period from each system's change records.
Obtain the configuration that refuses a conflicting assignment, and the log of refusals and diversions it produced.
Request the list of emergency and support roles with their holders and the expiry set on each.

Analysis:
Resolve every role in the catalogue to duties and compare the result with the matrix, so a role combining a pair inside itself is found.
Sample twenty-five assignments from the period and re-perform the check against what each user already held on the grant date.
Compare the mapping against a direct read of each role's authorisations, rather than relying on the description the mapping carries.
Attempt a deliberately conflicting assignment in a non-production copy to establish that the refusal actually fires.
Trace each emergency grant to an expiry and to the activity the holder produced while it was live.

Output:
Schedule of in-scope systems with the count of roles mapped and unmapped in each.
List of roles that internally complete a forbidden pair, with the number of holders of each.
Statement of whether the assignment refusal operated, evidenced by the attempt made and its result.
Exceptions where a grant completed a forbidden pair with no recorded acceptance behind it.

title.en: Name the systems whose roles carry a financial duty

description.en: Fix which applications, databases and interfaces grant the duties the matrix names, including the places a financial duty is performed outside the main ledger system.

text.en: Take the systems named in the significant account and process scoping.
Add anywhere a journal, payment or master record can be created or altered.
Note for each system who administers its roles and how a grant is made.
Mark the systems whose access is granted outside the identity platform.
Agree the resulting list with the control owner and the administrators.

title.en: Map each role to the duties its authorisations really grant

description.en: Resolve every role in each in-scope system down to the transactions and objects it can reach, then express that reach in the duty vocabulary the conflict matrix uses so the two can be compared at all.

text.en: Export the role catalogue and its underlying authorisations from each system.
Resolve each role to the transactions and records it can actually reach.
Translate that reach into the duty terms the conflict matrix uses.
Flag roles whose own contents already complete a forbidden pair.
Have the system administrator confirm the mapping matches the build.

title.en: Configure the assignment path to refuse a conflicting grant

description.en: Build the check into the way access is actually granted, through the request workflow or provisioning rules, so a conflicting combination is stopped at assignment instead of discovered by a scan months later.

text.en: Load the matrix pairs into the request or provisioning workflow.
Evaluate what the user already holds, not only the role being requested.
Stop the request, or divert it to the acceptance route, on a hit.
Split or rebuild the roles found to carry a forbidden pair inside them.
Prove the refusal fires by raising a deliberately conflicting request in test.

title.en: Check a role against the conflict matrix before any user holds it

description.en: Put every role build, role change and privileged grant through the conflict check as part of the change itself, so the design cannot drift between periodic scans.

evidenceHint.en: Change tickets for the period's role builds, changes and emergency grants, each carrying the check result, the matrix version used and the release decision taken.

text.en: Route each role build or change through the conflict check before release.
Note the result on the change ticket with the matrix version it used.
Hold the change where a pair is completed, until it is split or accepted.
Time-box emergency and support grants and set the withdrawal date at issue.
Reject a grant made outside the path and remove the access it created.

title.en: Re-perform the duty mapping on a sample of live roles

description.en: Take roles as they are configured today rather than as the mapping describes them and rebuild the duty picture independently, because a stale mapping makes enforcement and detection both look clean.

text.en: Select roles covering the severest duties and the largest holder counts.
Read each role's authorisations from the system itself, not the mapping.
Compare the rebuilt duty set with the mapping the control relies on.
Report the differences to the mapping owner and re-run detection after.
State whether the mapping can be relied on for the period under review.

templates.title: SoD conflicts detected and reported periodically
templates.description: A periodic search of live entitlements for the combinations the conflict matrix forbids, with what it finds put in front of the people who can remove, accept or mitigate each one.
templates.objective: To ensure live entitlements are searched each quarter for the combinations the matrix forbids, and that what the search returns reaches the people able to act on it while it is current.
templates.successCriteria:
The scan reads every in-scope system and every account type, contractors, shared, service and emergency identities included.
Detection rules are generated from the matrix version in force, and the version used is recorded beside the output.
A scan ran in each period, its output retained and reconcilable to the user population held at the run date.
The report names the conflicted individual, the pair held, the systems involved and how long the conflict has been open.
Every conflict leaves the period removed, accepted with a mitigation, or dismissed as a false positive with the reason recorded.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the scan output for each period of the year, with its run date and the matrix version the rules were built from.
Obtain the rule set the scan executes and the record of who is permitted to change it.
Draw the user population from each in-scope system as at a scan date, including contractor, shared and service accounts.
Collect the report issued to management for each period and the list of recipients it went to.
Request the disposition record for the conflicts each scan raised.

Analysis:
Reconcile the accounts the scan examined against the population drawn independently from each system, and quantify the shortfall.
Re-perform the detection for a sample of five pairs over the raw entitlement extract and compare the users returned with the scan's own list.
Compare rule and matrix version dates to test whether the rules were regenerated after the matrix last changed.
Trace every conflict raised by the first scan of the year to a removal, an acceptance or a dismissal, examining the reason given for ten dismissals.
Set each report's issue date against its scan date to judge whether it reached management while still current.

Output:
Schedule of the period's scans with run dates, matrix versions and the accounts each covered.
List of in-scope systems or account types absent from the scanned population.
Reconciliation of the re-performed detection against the scan's own output, with differences explained.
Ageing of conflicts open at period end, naming those carried from an earlier scan with no disposition.

title.en: Delimit the accounts and systems each scan must reach

description.en: Fix the population the scan will be measured against, every in-scope system and every kind of identity inside it, so that a clean result cannot be produced by a narrow search.

text.en: List the systems holding any duty the conflict matrix names.
Bring contractor, shared, service and emergency identities into the population.
Agree how that population will be evidenced at each run date.
Set the cadence and the date each period's scan falls due.
Name who receives the output and who is entitled to act on it.

title.en: Build the detection rules from the pairs the matrix forbids

description.en: Turn each forbidden pair into a query over role, entitlement and user data that returns the people holding both sides, and tie the rule set to the matrix version it was generated from.

text.en: Write one rule per pair, returning the users who hold both duties.
Resolve indirect holdings through nested groups and role hierarchies.
Stamp the rule set with the matrix version it was generated from.
Validate each rule against a test user planted to hold the pair.
Fix who may amend a rule, and require the matrix owner to agree it.

title.en: Run the scan and retain what it returned for the period

description.en: Execute the scan on its due date across the agreed population and keep the output, the population read and the rule version together, so the run can be re-performed later by someone else.

evidenceHint.en: Each period's scan output with its run date, rule and matrix versions, the account population read, and the raw entitlement extract it was produced from.

text.en: Execute the scan across every system in the agreed population.
Keep the raw entitlement extract beside the conflicts it produced.
Note the run date, the rule version and the count of accounts read.
Investigate any shortfall between accounts read and accounts expected.

title.en: Report the conflicts found with an age against each

description.en: Put the period's conflicts in front of the managers who own the people and the systems, showing who holds which pair and how many periods it has stood, so that what is old is visibly old.

evidenceHint.en: The issued report for each period, showing the conflicted individuals, the pair each holds, the age of every open conflict and the recipients it was sent to.

text.en: Name each conflicted individual, the pair held and the systems involved.
Age each conflict from the scan that first returned it.
Separate new conflicts from those carried since the previous period.
Issue the report to the named recipients inside the agreed days.
Present the summary to finance leadership at its next session.

title.en: Trace each detected conflict to what was done about it

description.en: Follow the output of each scan through to a removal, an acceptance or a dismissal, so detection is judged by what changed afterwards rather than by the fact a report was produced.

text.en: Match the previous scan's conflicts against the current scan's list.
Confirm a removed conflict is absent from the later entitlement extract.
Test that every acceptance carried an approval before the period closed.
Question dismissals that recur period after period as false positives.
Escalate conflicts open longer than the agreed limit to the control owner.

templates.title: Mitigating controls documented for accepted conflicts
templates.description: Where a forbidden combination is allowed to stand, a named compensating control is recorded against it, performed by someone clear of both duties, and the acceptance carries an approver and an expiry.
templates.objective: To ensure a conflict management chooses to live with carries a named mitigating control, an accountable approver and a date it expires, rather than standing as an unexamined exception.
templates.successCriteria:
Every accepted conflict exists as an exception record naming the pair, the individual holding it and the person who accepted the risk.
The exception names one specific mitigating control rather than general assurance, and its reviewer holds neither side of the pair.
The mitigating review ran in each period it fell due, over the transactions the conflicted person could actually touch.
Acceptance criteria name the pairs that may never be accepted, and no exception in the register carries one of them.
Each acceptance carries an expiry and was renewed, withdrawn or escalated before that date passed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the exception register of accepted conflicts in force during the period, showing the approver, the mitigating control and the expiry against each.
Obtain the acceptance criteria, including the pairs ruled never acceptable and the authority level each severity demands.
Draw the population of mitigating reviews falling due in the period from the register and the frequency each exception states.
Collect the output of each review performed: the transaction listing examined, who examined it and what they concluded.
Request the record of renewals, withdrawals and escalations taken at expiry.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against the conflicts the period's detection scans reported as accepted, and explain the extras on either side.
Test every exception against the acceptance criteria and list any naming a pair ruled never acceptable.
Examine each reviewer's independence from both duties using the role-to-duty mapping rather than job titles.
Sample fifteen reviews due in the period and test that each was performed, covered the holder's own transactions, and was evidenced.
Set each expiry against the renewal or withdrawal recorded, and quantify the acceptances that ran on past it.

Output:
Register extract of accepted conflicts with approver, mitigating control, reviewer and expiry for each.
List of exceptions carrying no mitigating control, no approver, or an expired acceptance still relied upon.
Schedule of reviews due and performed, with the exceptions sampled and the result of each.
Statement of whether any accepted conflict falls inside the never-acceptable set.

title.en: Qualify which conflicts may be accepted and which never can

description.en: Decide ahead of any request which pairs an acceptance can cover and which it can never cover, and fix who holds authority to accept each severity, so acceptance is a rule rather than a negotiation.

text.en: Take the severity grade recorded against each pair in the matrix.
Rule out acceptance for pairs reaching cash or the ledger unchecked.
Set the authority level entitled to accept each remaining severity.
State the maximum term an acceptance may run before it must be renewed.
Publish the criteria alongside the conflict matrix they belong to.

title.en: Name the compensating control that covers each acceptance

description.en: Set against every acceptance one control that would detect what the conflict permits, performed by somebody holding neither duty, at a stated frequency and over a stated population.

text.en: Choose a control that would detect the misstatement the pair permits.
Check the reviewer holds neither duty, using the role-to-duty mapping.
State the population it covers and the frequency it must run at.
Raise the exception record naming the control, the approver and the expiry.
Link that exception to the compensating control the register already holds.

title.en: Operate the mitigating review over what the holder can touch

description.en: Run each mitigating review on its due date over the transactions the conflicted person actually initiated or altered, keeping what the reviewer saw and questioned rather than the conclusion alone.

evidenceHint.en: For each acceptance, the completed review for the period: the transaction listing examined, the reviewer's name and date, the items questioned and the outcome of each.

text.en: Extract the conflicted person's transactions for the period under review.
Have the independent reviewer examine them against the stated criteria.
Note what was questioned and how each question was answered.
Sign and date the review, naming the exception it was performed for.
Escalate anything the review cannot explain to the person who accepted the risk.

title.en: Refresh or withdraw each acceptance before its expiry falls

description.en: Bring every acceptance back to its approver ahead of the expiry date with what the mitigating reviews have found since it was granted, so a temporary tolerance cannot become permanent by silence.

evidenceHint.en: The expiry schedule for the period showing each acceptance falling due, the decision taken, the approver and the date, with the superseded record each renewal replaced.

text.en: Track expiries and warn the approver ahead of each one falling due.
Assemble the review results produced since the acceptance was granted.
Put the renewal, withdrawal or escalation decision to that approver.
Close the exception and remove the access where renewal is refused.
Carry the renewal lineage forward so the history stays readable.

title.en: Judge whether each mitigation covers what the conflict permits

description.en: Challenge the register independently by taking a conflicted holder, working out what they could do undetected, and testing whether the named mitigating control would in fact have caught it.

text.en: Select the acceptances covering the severest pairs in the register.
Work out what the holder could do that the mitigation would not see.
Test the reviewer's independence against the current role mapping.
Examine whether the reviews were performed every period they fell due.
Refer inadequate mitigations to the risk acceptor for withdrawal.

templates.title: Review precision criteria defined per review control
templates.description: A written specification for each management review control stating the data examined, the comparison it is set against, and the size of difference that forces an investigation.
templates.objective: To ensure each management review control carries a written precision specification naming the data examined, the comparison basis, and the difference large enough to force an investigation.
templates.successCriteria:
Every control identified as a management review carries a precision specification naming the report, its disaggregation and the comparison basis.
Each specification states an investigation threshold as an amount or a percentage, with the materiality figure it was derived from.
The specification names who performs the review, who an unexplained item goes to, and the period it must complete within.
The specification in force on the date of any past review can be produced, not only the current version.
A threshold amended during the period records the reason for the change and the person who approved it.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the key control listing and the subset flagged as management review controls, exported at the date of test.
Obtain the precision specification held for each review control in that subset, with its version date and approver.
Obtain the performance materiality figure for the period and the working paper deriving it.
Request the change history for any threshold amended during the period under test.

Analysis:
Reconcile specifications held against the review controls on the key control listing, and list the controls holding none.
Sample twelve specifications, or all where fewer, and test that each names a report, a disaggregation level, a comparison basis and a numeric threshold.
Recalculate each sampled threshold against performance materiality and flag any that sits above it with no rationale recorded.
Set each specification's version date against the reviews it governed, to find reviews performed before any specification existed.
Read thresholds worded as judgement - significant, unusual, material - and treat each as unspecified rather than as a threshold.

Output:
State how many review controls hold a precision specification, and name the ones that do not.
List sampled specifications missing a report, a disaggregation level, a comparison basis or a numeric threshold.
Report thresholds above performance materiality with no rationale, giving the amount of each.
Name the reviews performed in a period no specification covered.

title.en: Inventory the review controls whose conclusion rests on judgement

description.en: Work through the key control listing and pull out the controls where a person reads a report and decides whether it is right, because those are the ones a precision specification has to exist for.

text.en: Pull the current key control listing and mark every control performed by a person reading a report.
Separate reviews that recompute a figure from reviews that only confirm a report was produced.
Record for each one the report it uses and the system that report is drawn from.
Rank the shortlist by the size of the balance or transaction flow each review sits over.
Issue the shortlist as the population that must carry a precision specification.

title.en: Derive each investigation threshold from performance materiality

description.en: Set the number that forces an investigation by working down from the period's performance materiality and the volume of items the review covers, rather than accepting the figure the reviewer has always used.

text.en: Take the performance materiality figure agreed for the period as the starting point.
Divide it across the reviews covering the same account so their thresholds cannot aggregate above it.
Express the threshold as an absolute amount and, where the balance moves, as a percentage.
Run the proposed threshold over last period's errors and record how many of them it would have raised.
Record the approver of each threshold and the date from which it takes effect.

title.en: Publish the precision specification the reviewer must work to

description.en: Issue the agreed specification to the named reviewer before the period it governs opens, so the person doing the work knows the threshold in advance rather than defending one after the fact.

evidenceHint.en: The issued specification carrying its effective date, the named performer and escalation point, and the acknowledgement returned by the reviewer it was sent to.

text.en: Send the specification to the named reviewer before the first period it governs.
Attach the report layout the review is to be performed on, at the stated disaggregation.
State the escalation route for an item above the threshold that cannot be explained.
Collect the reviewer's acknowledgement that the threshold and the route are understood.
Store the issued version so the specification in force on any review date can be produced.

title.en: Challenge whether the threshold would have caught the errors found

description.en: Take the misstatements, audit adjustments and late corrections the period actually produced, and measure each against the threshold in force at the time to see whether the review was ever capable of finding it.

text.en: Assemble the period's audit adjustments, corrections and known misstatements with their amounts.
Match each one to the review control that should have detected it first.
Compare the amount against the threshold that was in force on that date.
Record every case where the error sat below the threshold and so could never have been raised.
Lower the thresholds those cases expose and route the change through approval.

templates.title: Review evidence retained including outlier follow-up
templates.description: The record a performed review leaves behind: the report version examined, the items that breached the threshold, the question put to each of them, and the answer that closed it.
templates.objective: To ensure a performed management review leaves a record showing what was examined, which items exceeded the threshold, and how each of those items was pursued to an answer.
templates.successCriteria:
Each performed review retains the report version it examined, identified by run date and the parameters used.
Items exceeding the investigation threshold appear individually, with their own amount and account, rather than as a described group.
For every such item the record holds the question asked, the explanation received and the document that corroborates it.
The record carries the reviewer's identity and the sign-off date, distinct from the date the report was produced.
Where an explanation was accepted without supporting documents, the reviewer recorded why it was sufficient.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the reviews scheduled in the period for the review controls in scope, and the log of those actually performed.
Obtain the retained workpaper for each review selected, together with the underlying report as it was run.
Obtain the precision specification in force, so the items that should have been treated as outliers are known.
Request the system-held sign-off dates, which sit outside the workpaper and cannot be typed into it.

Analysis:
Reconcile reviews performed against reviews scheduled, by control, and quantify the shortfall.
Select twenty-five performed reviews across the period, weighted to period-end and to the highest-value accounts.
Apply the specification's threshold to the retained report and list items that met it yet appear nowhere in the workpaper.
For each outlier the workpaper does carry, test whether it records a question, an answer and a corroborating document.
Compare sign-off dates with report run dates to find reviews signed before the data existed or well after the close window.

Output:
State reviews performed against reviews scheduled, by control and by month.
List outliers present in the data and absent from the review record, with their amounts.
Report outliers accepted on explanation alone, naming the reviewer and the item.
Name reviews whose sign-off date precedes the report run date or falls outside the close window.

title.en: Delimit what a complete review record has to contain

description.en: Agree before any review is performed the minimum the workpaper must hold - report version, itemised outliers, the enquiry and its answer - so completeness becomes a checkable property rather than a matter of taste.

text.en: List the fields the workpaper must carry, starting with the report version and its run parameters.
Require outliers to be itemised, each one with its own amount and account.
Define what counts as corroboration, and what is only the preparer repeating themselves.
Set the retention period and the location the completed record is filed in.
Circulate the minimum set to every reviewer it will apply to.

title.en: Configure the workpaper so an unexplained outlier blocks sign-off

description.en: Put the control into the template itself: a review cannot reach sign-off while an itemised outlier has an empty explanation or no attachment, so the gap surfaces at the point it is still cheap to fix.

text.en: Add an outlier table to the template, populated from the report rather than typed by hand.
Make the explanation and corroboration fields mandatory on every populated row.
Block the sign-off action while any row remains incomplete, showing the reason it is blocked.
Stamp the report run date and parameters into the workpaper automatically.
Pilot the template over one close before issuing it to every reviewer.

title.en: Capture the enquiry made of each outlier and the answer accepted

description.en: As the review runs, write down for every item over the threshold what was asked, who answered it, what was produced to support that answer, and whether it was accepted or pushed back for more.

evidenceHint.en: The completed workpaper for the period, showing every itemised outlier with its enquiry, the person who responded, the supporting document and the acceptance decision.

text.en: Pull the outlier list straight from the report at the disaggregation the specification names.
Record against each item the question put and the person it was put to.
Attach the document that supports the answer, not a note of the conversation.
Mark items pushed back for a second answer and carry them until they settle.
Sign the record on the date the last item closed, not the date the review opened.

title.en: Re-perform a signed review from the retained record alone

description.en: Take a completed review and try to reach the same conclusion using only what was kept: if the record does not let an independent person repeat the work, the evidence is insufficient whatever the sign-off says.

text.en: Choose signed reviews from across the period and from more than one reviewer.
Re-run the report at the version and parameters the retained record names.
Apply the threshold again and compare the outliers found with the ones on file.
Read each recorded answer and judge whether the attached support actually proves it.
Report the reviews that cannot be repeated from the record, naming what was missing.

templates.title: Items arising from management review resolved and closed
templates.description: The residue of a review: every question that turned out to need an action is driven to a closed state evidenced by the corrected record, not by the status field on a log.
templates.objective: To ensure every item a management review raises is driven to closure within a stated window and evidenced by the corrected record, rather than carried forward from one review to the next.
templates.successCriteria:
Items are logged individually against the review that raised them, with the account affected and the date raised.
Every open item carries a named person as owner and a closure date set when it was raised, not when it was chased.
Closure is supported by the corrected journal, reconciliation or amended procedure, not by a status field alone.
Items still open past their closure date are reported to the level above the owner on a stated cadence.
The same item recurring across consecutive reviews is escalated as a design problem rather than simply reopened.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the item log for every review control in scope, exported at the date of test with raised, due and closed dates.
Obtain the underlying review records for the period, so items raised can be reconciled to items logged.
Obtain the closure evidence attached to items marked closed: journals, reconciliations, amended procedures.
Request the overdue-item escalation reports issued in the period and the distribution list of each.

Analysis:
Reconcile items raised in the sampled review records against items on the log, and quantify those raised but never logged.
Sample thirty closed items, or all where fewer, weighted toward the largest amounts and the longest open durations.
Test each sampled closure against its supporting document, treating a status change with no document as still open.
Measure days from raised to closed against the stated window, and profile the ageing of the items still open.
Group items by description to find the same issue raised in consecutive periods, and check whether escalation followed.

Output:
State items raised, closed and open at the date of test, by review control.
List items raised in a review record that never reached the log.
Report closures unsupported by a corrected record, with the amount and the owner of each.
Name recurring items reopened rather than escalated, with the number of periods each has run.

title.en: Open a single item log that every management review feeds

description.en: Decide where an item goes the moment a review raises one, so a question that needed an action cannot live in a reviewer's inbox or in the margin of a workpaper nobody reads again.

text.en: Name one log as the place items from every review control are recorded.
Fix the fields it holds: source review, account, amount, owner, raised date and due date.
Define what closure means for each type of item, and which document proves it.
Set the window an item has to run before it counts as overdue.
Retire the side lists reviewers were keeping and migrate their open items across.

title.en: Route each raised item to a named owner with a closure date

description.en: Attach ownership at the point the item is raised rather than at the point it is chased: the reviewer names the person who can actually fix it and the date it must be finished by, before signing the review.

text.en: Require the reviewer to name an owner before the item can be saved.
Set the due date from that item type's window, measured from the raised date.
Notify the owner and their manager on the day the item is raised.
Reject items assigned to a team or a function rather than to a person.
Carry the amount and the account onto the item so its size stays visible.

title.en: Chase open items to closure before the next review runs

description.en: Work the log between reviews: pursue the owner of each open item, record what moved, and bring in the closure evidence rather than accepting a verbal assurance that the matter is in hand.

evidenceHint.en: The item log exported ahead of each review, showing per item the chase history, the closure document attached, and the date the item was accepted as closed.

text.en: Export the open items a week before the next review of that control.
Contact each owner for a position and record the date and the answer given.
Attach the corrected journal or amended procedure as each item closes.
Refuse closure where the document does not cover the item's full amount.
Carry the items still open into the next review's agenda by name.

title.en: Verify closure against the corrected record, not the log status

description.en: Independently reopen a sample of items the log calls closed and follow each one into the ledger, the reconciliation or the procedure, because a closed status is the claim and the corrected record is the proof.

text.en: Select closed items spanning owners, amounts and ages from the period's log.
Trace each into the ledger, reconciliation or procedure it claims to have corrected.
Confirm the correction covers the period and the amount the item described.
Reopen items whose evidence does not reach the amount claimed, and say so in writing.
Report the recurring items that closed and came back, with the periods each spans.

templates.title: Close calendar and checklist maintained and executed
templates.description: A dated task list for each period-end close, every task carrying an owner, a due point and the tasks it depends on, worked through in order and signed off so the ledger closes on a schedule rather than when the work happens to finish.
templates.objective: To ensure every period-end close task is scheduled with an owner and a due point, worked in dependency order, and signed off before the ledger is locked for reporting.
templates.successCriteria:
A close calendar exists for the period, listing each task with its owner, its due point and the tasks it depends on.
Every task carries a completion record naming the person who performed it and the time it finished, rather than a tick against a department.
The posting period is locked on the date the calendar fixes, and any extension of that date carries a recorded approval.
Tasks finished after their due point are visible as late, with the reason recorded and the downstream work they delayed named.
New accounts, entities and systems are attached to a calendar task before the first close in which they report.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the close calendar in force for the three closes selected; the population is every task it lists, typically 60 to 120 per close.
Collect the completed checklist instances for those closes, each carrying the performer and the completion time against every task.
Request the system log of posting-period lock and unlock events for the same three closes.
Obtain the approvals for any extension of a lock date and the finance team's own record of late tasks.
Collect the prior period calendar and the change record between it and the version in force.

Analysis:
Reconcile the task list against the completed instances in full for one close, so an omitted task is visible rather than sampled around.
Sample fifteen tasks across the three closes, weighted to those feeding consolidation, tax and disclosure, and compare completion times with due points.
Set each lock event against the date the calendar fixed and confirm every unlock afterwards carries an approval.
Test whether the performer recorded could have done the task, rather than the checklist owner closing entries centrally.
Trace accounts, entities and systems new in the period to the calendar task that covers them.

Output:
Count of calendar tasks with no completion record, by close and by owner.
Schedule of tasks finished after their due point, with the downstream work each one delayed.
Statement of whether the ledger locked on the fixed date at each close, with the approval behind any extension.
List of new accounts, entities and systems reporting with no calendar task covering them.

title.en: Enumerate the work a close consists of, from cutoff to lock

description.en: Establish what a complete close actually contains by walking the period end from the last subledger cutoff through to the locked ledger, writing down every task performed on the way.

text.en: Walk the last close with each subledger owner and list the tasks they performed.
Add the work done centrally: accruals, allocations, revaluation and the lock itself.
Mark the tasks whose output feeds consolidation, tax or the disclosure drafting.
Record which tasks depend on which, so a delay shows what it holds up.
Name the accounts and entities each task covers, so a new one has somewhere to attach.

title.en: Time each task to a due point and a named performer

description.en: Turn the task list into a calendar a finance team can work to, with every task dated relative to close day one, assigned to an individual, and bounded by the lock date reporting depends on.

text.en: Fix each task's due point as a day and hour relative to close day one.
Assign every task to an individual rather than to a team mailbox.
Set the date the posting period locks and the approval needed to move it.
Circulate the draft to subledger owners so an unworkable date is challenged before issue.

title.en: Run the checklist through the close and sign each task off

description.en: Work the calendar in order at every close, recording who performed each task and when it finished, and escalating a task heading for a miss before it delays the ones behind it.

evidenceHint.en: The completed checklist instance for the period, carrying a performer and a completion time against every line, filed with the close pack.

text.en: Open an instance of the checklist for the close from the approved calendar.
Record the performer and the completion time against each task as it finishes.
Escalate a task heading for a missed due point before the miss occurs.
Lock the posting period on the fixed date, or obtain approval to extend it.
File the completed instance with the close pack as the period's evidence.

title.en: Grade the closes on what ran late and what was never listed

description.en: Look back across the period's closes and judge whether the calendar described the work honestly: which tasks slipped, which were performed off-calendar, and which new reporting units arrived without one.

text.en: Compare the completed instances against the calendar to find tasks never performed.
Identify work done during the close that no calendar task covers.
Measure how late each slipped task was and what it delayed downstream.
Amend the calendar for new accounts, entities and systems before the next close.

templates.title: Journal entries reviewed and approved independently
templates.description: Manual journal entries are put to someone other than the person who wrote them, tested against the support they cite before they reach a reported balance, and any entry that posted without that approval is found and explained.
templates.objective: To ensure each manual journal entry is approved by someone independent of its preparer, against the support it cites, before the posting affects a reported balance.
templates.successCriteria:
Manual entries are identified separately from system-generated postings at source, rather than by inspection after the ledger has closed.
Each manual entry above the review threshold carries an approver who neither prepared nor posted it.
The approval is dated before the entry affects a reported balance and names the support the approver relied on.
Post-close and top-side entries are approved at a level above the ordinary threshold whatever their value.
Users able to approve their own postings are listed, and every entry they raise is reviewed by a second person.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Extract every journal posted in the period with preparer, approver, source, value and posting time; this is the population, and manual entries are the stratum tested.
Obtain the configured review threshold and the list of users holding journal approval rights.
Collect the approval records for the sampled entries together with the documents each approval cites.
Request the role configuration showing which users can both raise and release a posting.
Obtain the log of post-close and top-side entries for every close in the period.

Analysis:
Reconcile the journal extract to the movement in the general ledger, so the population is known to be complete rather than merely supplied.
Test all manual entries above the threshold and all post-close entries, and sample twenty-five below it stratified by preparer and by close.
Compare preparer and approver on every item tested and treat a match as an exception without regard to value.
Set each approval time against the posting time to find approvals given after the entry reached the ledger.
Vouch each sampled entry to the support its approval names and judge whether that document evidences the amount.

Output:
Population and sample sizes with the strata used, so coverage can be judged rather than assumed.
List of entries where preparer and approver are the same person or the same shared account.
Schedule of approvals dated after posting, with the elapsed time and value on each.
Exceptions where the cited support does not carry the posted amount, with the balances affected.

title.en: Delimit which postings are manual and which the system raises

description.en: Separate the postings a person writes from those a system generates, then set the value and type thresholds that decide which of them attract an independent approval.

text.en: Classify every journal source in the ledger as manual, interfaced or automatic.
Set the value above which a manual posting attracts independent approval.
Name the entry types reviewed at any value, including top-side and post-close.
Identify the accounts where a manual posting is itself unusual enough to review.

title.en: Configure the routing so a preparer cannot release their own posting

description.en: Put the independence requirement into the ledger itself, so the approval route is enforced by configuration instead of depending on what the preparer chooses to do at posting time.

text.en: Route entries above the threshold to an approver queue before they post.
Remove the ability to release an own posting from every preparer role.
Require the approver to record the support relied on before releasing.
Capture preparer, approver and both timestamps on the entry record itself.

title.en: Approve each in-scope entry against the support it cites

description.en: Perform the review itself: read what the entry claims to do, test the figure against the document behind it, and either release it or return it, inside the window the close calendar allows.

evidenceHint.en: The released journal showing its approver, the time of release and the document relied on, held with the close pack for the period.

text.en: Read the narrative and judge whether it explains why the entry is needed.
Agree the amount to the document the preparer attached to it.
