Return any entry whose support does not carry the posted figure.
Release within the close window so the entry is not posted late.

title.en: Search the ledger for postings that never passed a reviewer

description.en: Test the control from the ledger's side rather than the approval queue's, finding entries that reached a reported balance with no approval and establishing the route by which each one got there.

text.en: Extract every posting in the period with its approval status attached.
Isolate entries above the threshold carrying no approver or a self-release.
Trace each exception to what allowed it, whether configuration or emergency access.
Report the exceptions with their value and the balances they reached.

templates.title: Account reconciliations prepared and reviewed on cycle
templates.description: Each account on the reconciliation inventory is agreed to an independent source on its stated cycle, reviewed by someone other than the preparer, and its reconciling items cleared within an age limit rather than carried forward indefinitely.
templates.objective: To ensure every account on the reconciliation inventory is agreed to an independent source on its cycle, reviewed independently of its preparer, and its open items cleared within a stated age.
templates.successCriteria:
A reconciliation inventory names every account carrying a balance, with its owner, its cycle and the source it is agreed to.
Each reconciliation agrees the ledger balance to that source, with the difference itemised rather than shown as a net figure.
A reviewer other than the preparer signs each reconciliation within the days the close calendar allows for it.
Open items carry an age, an owner and a clearing action, and anything beyond the age limit is escalated rather than rolled.
Accounts on the trial balance appearing on no reconciliation are added to the inventory or excluded on a recorded basis.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the reconciliation inventory and the trial balance at period end; together they define the population, which is every account carrying a balance.
Collect the completed reconciliations for the periods selected, with the preparer and reviewer sign-offs and their dates.
Request the independent sources behind the sampled accounts: bank statements, custodian reports, subledger extracts and counterparty confirmations.
Obtain the open item log showing the age of every unresolved reconciling item.
Collect the close calendar entries that fix when each reconciliation falls due.

Analysis:
Reconcile the inventory against the trial balance in full, listing accounts with a balance and no reconciliation and inventory entries with no balance.
Sample thirty reconciliations weighted to cash, intercompany, suspense, accrual and any account carrying a prior period exception.
Agree the ledger figure on each sampled reconciliation to the trial balance and the source figure to the independent document behind it.
Compare preparer and reviewer identities, and set each sign-off date against the calendar date it was due.
Age the open items on the sampled accounts and test whether those past the limit were escalated or simply carried.

Output:
Schedule of accounts with a balance but no reconciliation, and of reconciliations for accounts no longer in use.
Sample results by account type, stating how many were tested and what was found in each.
List of reconciliations signed by the preparer alone, or reviewed after the date the calendar set.
Aged analysis of open reconciling items, naming those beyond the limit and the owner of each.

title.en: Inventory the accounts to be reconciled, and to what source

description.en: Draw the reconciliation population from the trial balance rather than from habit, settling for each account the independent source it will be agreed to and how often that has to happen.

text.en: List every account carrying a balance at the period end.
Name the independent source each account will be agreed to.
Set the cycle for each account: monthly, quarterly or on movement.
Record a basis for every account left out of the inventory.
Assign a preparer and a separate reviewer to each account.

title.en: Draft a reconciliation format that itemises the difference

description.en: Give preparers one format that forces the difference to be broken into items with owners and dates, so an unexplained balance cannot hide inside a single summarised line.

text.en: Show the ledger balance and the source balance side by side.
Break the difference into items, each with a date, a cause and an owner.
Carry the age of every open item forward from the prior period.
Provide dated sign-off blocks for the preparer and the reviewer.

title.en: Prepare each reconciliation inside the days the calendar allows

description.en: Perform the reconciliation on cycle: agree both sides to their sources as at the same date, itemise whatever remains, and put it to the reviewer before it falls due.

evidenceHint.en: The signed reconciliation for the account and period, showing both balances agreed to their sources with the itemised difference attached.

text.en: Pull the ledger balance and the independent source as at the same date.
Itemise every difference rather than presenting a net amount.
Attach the document supporting each item above the threshold.
Submit the reconciliation to the reviewer by the date it falls due.

title.en: Close out the open items before they pass the age limit

description.en: Work the open items instead of rolling them forward, chasing each to the action that clears it and escalating whatever survives the age limit rather than letting it enter another period.

evidenceHint.en: The aged open item log for the period, showing each item's age, its owner, the action taken and the escalations raised past the limit.

text.en: Age every unresolved item from the date it first arose.
Assign each item to the person able to clear it.
Escalate anything past the age limit to the account owner's manager.
Write off or provide for items that cannot be cleared, with approval.

title.en: Compare the inventory against the trial balance at period end

description.en: Test the completeness of the population itself, which no individual reconciliation can demonstrate: an account carrying a balance and appearing on no reconciliation is the gap this looks for.

text.en: Match every trial balance account to an entry in the inventory.
List accounts holding a balance for which nothing was reconciled.
Identify inventory entries for accounts no longer used.
Refer unreconciled balances to the controller with their value.

templates.title: Significant estimates and judgements reviewed
templates.description: Each estimate the statements depend on carries a written methodology and inputs that can be traced outside the model, is reviewed for the judgement it embodies rather than its arithmetic, and is compared afterwards against what actually settled.
templates.objective: To ensure each significant estimate rests on a recorded methodology and traceable inputs, is challenged independently before posting, and is measured afterwards against the amount that settled.
templates.successCriteria:
A register lists every significant estimate with its methodology, its key inputs and the individual accountable for the figure.
The methodology applied in the period is the one recorded, and any change to it carries a stated reason and an approval.
Every key input can be traced to a source outside the model that computes the estimate.
The reviewer records the range considered and why the point selected sits where it does, not merely that the figure was approved.
Prior estimates are measured against the amounts that settled, and a difference falling consistently one way is reported rather than absorbed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of significant estimates; the population is every estimate carrying a stated methodology, typically credit loss allowances, inventory and warranty provisions, impairment, incentive accruals and tax positions.
Collect the working papers behind the estimates selected, including the model, its inputs and the version approved for the period.
Request the reviewer's note showing the range considered and the basis on which the point was selected.
Obtain the prior period estimates together with the amounts that have since settled against them.
Collect the approvals for any change of methodology or key assumption during the period.

Analysis:
Test every estimate whose value exceeds performance materiality and sample three below it, so the population is covered by value rather than by count.
Trace each key input to its source: the aged debt listing, the claims history, the rate published externally, the forecast the board approved.
Re-perform the calculation on one estimate per method to confirm the model applies the methodology recorded for it.
Compare the assumptions used against the prior period and against the approved forecast, investigating any movement with no stated cause.
Measure at least two prior estimates against what settled and judge the direction of the difference on each.

Output:
Population of estimates with the value of each, and the sample selected with the basis on which it was chosen.
Exceptions where the methodology applied differs from the one recorded, with the effect on the figure reported.
List of key inputs that could not be traced beyond the model that consumed them.
Table of estimate, outcome and difference by period, naming any bias that runs consistently one way.

title.en: Catalogue the figures that rest on judgement, and their drivers

description.en: Identify which amounts in the statements depend on judgement rather than measurement, recording for each the driver that moves it most and the individual accountable for the number.

text.en: List the balances and charges that depend on a judgement.
Record the driver that moves each of them most.
Name the individual accountable for the figure, not the team.
Rank them by value against performance materiality.

title.en: Document the methodology and the inputs behind each estimate

description.en: Write down how each estimate is computed and where its inputs come from, so the figure can be re-performed by someone who did not build the model that produces it.

text.en: State the method, the population and the period each estimate covers.
Name the source system or document behind every key input.
Record each assumption and the range it was selected from.
Version the model and record who approved the version in use.

title.en: Challenge the assumptions before the figure enters the ledger

description.en: Conduct the review as a challenge to the judgement rather than a check of the arithmetic, testing whether the assumptions still hold and recording the range considered before anything is posted.

evidenceHint.en: The reviewer's note for the period, stating the range considered, the point selected and the reason, signed and dated ahead of posting.

text.en: Compare each assumption against the evidence available at the reporting date.
Compute the figure at both ends of the reasonable range before accepting a point.
Record why the selected point sits where it does within that range.
Return the estimate to its preparer where an assumption cannot be supported.

title.en: Back-test prior estimates against the amounts that settled

description.en: Look at estimates whose outcome is now known and judge whether the method produces figures that land near the truth, or drifts consistently in one direction period after period.

text.en: Select estimates from earlier periods whose outcome has now settled.
Measure each recorded figure against the amount finally realised.
Judge whether the differences fall on one side across periods.
Refer a persistent bias to the audit committee with the method behind it.

templates.title: Consolidation and intercompany eliminations performed
templates.description: Component results enter the group at the approved ownership and rate, intercompany balances and trading are matched between the two entities that recorded them, and whatever remains after elimination is resolved rather than posted to a plug.
templates.objective: To ensure components consolidate on the approved structure, ownership and rates, with intercompany positions matched between counterparties and eliminated leaving no unexplained difference.
templates.successCriteria:
Every entity inside the boundary submits on the group chart, and each submission is agreed to that component's own ledger.
Intercompany balances and trading are matched pair by pair, and a difference above tolerance is resolved before elimination.
Each elimination journal is supported by the matched position it removes, with no balancing entry that lacks a counterparty.
Ownership percentages, translation rates and non-controlling interests agree to the source the board approved.
The group figures are agreed back to the components plus the adjustments posted, and that schedule is reviewed at group level.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the consolidation structure for the period; the population is every entity inside the boundary, each with its ownership percentage and functional currency.
Collect the component submissions and the reconciliation of each one to the component's own ledger.
Request the intercompany matching report showing every counterparty pair and the difference standing on each.
Obtain the elimination and adjustment journals posted at group level, with the support behind each.
Collect the rate table used for translation and the published source it was taken from.

Analysis:
Reconcile the consolidated entity list to the legal entity register in full, so an entity omitted from the group is visible rather than assumed absent.
Test every intercompany pair whose difference exceeds tolerance, and sample ten pairs below it to confirm matching actually took place.
Agree the ownership percentage and translation rate for eight entities chosen by value and by currency exposure.
Re-perform the addition from component submissions through eliminations to the group figure for one primary statement.
Examine every group-level adjustment for support, treating one that balances to a suspense or plug account as an exception.

Output:
Statement of whether the consolidated entity list matches the legal entity register, naming any difference either way.
Schedule of intercompany differences by pair, with the value, the age and the counterparty answerable for each.
Exceptions in ownership, rate or non-controlling interest, with the effect of each on the group figures.
List of group adjustments lacking support, including any posted to a plug or suspense account.

title.en: Scope the entities consolidated and the pairs trading between them

description.en: Fix the consolidation population before the close: which entities come in, at what ownership, in which currency, and which counterparty pairs will have positions needing to be matched.

text.en: List each entity inside the boundary with its ownership percentage.
Record the functional currency and the rate source for each component.
Identify the counterparty pairs that trade or hold balances with each other.
Set the tolerance above which a pair difference must be resolved.

title.en: Establish the group chart and the rules that remove each pair

description.en: Put the mapping and elimination logic into the consolidation system itself, so components report on one chart and intercompany positions are removed by rule rather than by a manual journal at the top.

text.en: Map each component's local accounts onto the group chart.
Define the elimination rule for every intercompany account pair.
Load the approved rate table and ownership percentages into the tool.
Restrict who may post a manual adjustment at group level.

title.en: Match the intercompany positions and resolve what differs

description.en: Run the matching between counterparties before the consolidation closes and make the two sides agree with each other, rather than letting the difference disappear into an elimination.

evidenceHint.en: The matching report for the period, showing each counterparty pair, the difference before and after resolution, and the journals that cleared it.

text.en: Circulate the matching report to both sides of every pair.
Require the counterparties to agree a difference or state its cause.
Post the correcting entries in the component ledgers, not at the top.
Escalate a pair still outside tolerance to the group controller.

title.en: Consolidate the components and agree the group figures back

description.en: Perform the consolidation itself and prove the result, so the group figures follow from the components plus the adjustments posted, with each adjustment traceable to the support behind it.

evidenceHint.en: The consolidation pack for the period, carrying the component-to-group reconciliation and every elimination and adjustment journal with its support.

text.en: Load each component submission and confirm it ties to the local ledger.
Post the eliminations and record the support behind each one.
Agree the group total to the components plus the adjustments posted.
Investigate any balancing entry with no counterparty behind it.

title.en: Examine the adjustments posted above component level

description.en: Look at what was added at the top rather than in the components, because a group-level adjustment is the entry least likely to have been seen by anyone outside the consolidation team.

text.en: List every journal posted at group level during the period.
Test each one for its support and for the approval it required.
Identify adjustments repeated each period with no stated cause.
Report entries posted to a plug or suspense account with their value.

templates.title: Disclosures reviewed against a disclosure checklist
templates.description: The statements and notes are worked through line by line against a current disclosure checklist, each answer tied to the note that satisfies it or to a recorded reason for not applying, and re-performed independently before approval.
templates.objective: To ensure the statements are worked against a current disclosure checklist line by line, with every answer tied to the note supporting it and re-performed independently before approval.
templates.successCriteria:
The checklist edition matches the framework and the reporting date, including pronouncements effective for the first time.
Every line carries an answer, and an answer of not applicable carries the reason it does not apply to the entity.
Each applicable line names the note, caption or page satisfying it, so the answer can be verified rather than assumed.
A reviewer independent of the preparer re-performs a defined portion of the checklist before the statements are approved.
Lines answered affirmatively but unsupported by the draft, and disclosures that no line called for, are both resolved before filing.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the completed disclosure checklist for the reporting date; the population is every line in it, and the sample is drawn from those answered as applicable.
Collect the draft statements as they stood when the checklist was completed, and the version finally approved.
Request the source and issue date of the checklist edition, with the list of pronouncements first effective this period.
Obtain the preparer and reviewer sign-offs with their dates, together with the reviewer's re-performance notes.
Collect the minute of the committee or board that approved the statements.

Analysis:
Compare the checklist edition against the framework in force and confirm it covers standards first effective in the period.
Sample forty applicable lines weighted to new pronouncements, judgement-heavy notes and areas restated since the prior year.
Trace each sampled line to the note or caption it names and judge whether that text actually satisfies the requirement.
Test every line answered not applicable in an area where the entity carries a balance, treating an unexplained answer as an exception.
Work the other direction on one primary statement: take each note in the draft and find the line that called for it.

Output:
Population of checklist lines by answer type, with the sample size and the basis on which it was selected.
Exceptions where the cited note does not support the answer given, naming the requirement involved.
List of not applicable answers carrying no reason, and those contradicted by a balance in the accounts.
Statement of whether the reviewer's sign-off preceded the approval of the statements, with any that did not.

title.en: Select the checklist edition matching the framework in force

description.en: Start from the right instrument: the edition tied to the framework the statements are prepared under, the reporting date reached, and the standards becoming effective for the first time this period.

text.en: Confirm the framework and version the statements are prepared under.
Obtain the checklist edition issued for that framework and date.
Add lines for pronouncements first effective in this period.
Remove sections for transactions the entity does not enter, with a reason.

title.en: Assign each checklist section to a preparer and a reviewer

description.en: Divide the checklist so every section has someone who answers it and someone else who tests the answer, with the dates both of them must meet fixed against the reporting calendar.

text.en: Split the checklist into sections by note and by statement.
Name a preparer for each section from the reporting team.
Name an independent reviewer for the portion to be re-performed.
Set the dates both must meet before the statements go for approval.

title.en: Complete every line against the draft and cite what satisfies it

description.en: Work through the checklist against the drafted statements, recording for each applicable line the note that satisfies it and for each exclusion the reason the entity does not reach it.

evidenceHint.en: The completed checklist for the reporting date, every line carrying its answer, the reference cited and the preparer and reviewer sign-offs.

text.en: Answer each line against the draft as it currently stands.
Cite the note, caption or page number that satisfies the line.
State the reason behind every answer of not applicable.
Raise a drafting action where the draft does not yet satisfy a line.
Sign the section off and pass it to the named reviewer.

title.en: Test the answers back against the statements finally approved

description.en: Check the checklist against the document that was actually approved rather than the draft it was completed on, looking in both directions so a note with no line is found as readily as a line with no note.

text.en: Re-perform a sample of lines against the approved statements.
Identify notes in the statements that no checklist line called for.
Confirm late drafting changes were re-checked after the answer was given.
Report unresolved lines to the disclosure committee before filing.

templates.title: Policy framework approved with defined ownership
templates.description: The set of written policies through which control activities are carried into practice, each approved by someone with authority over its subject and held by one named owner.
templates.objective: To ensure every policy the control framework leans on is approved by someone with authority over its subject and carries one named owner accountable for keeping it current.
templates.successCriteria:
The register holds a row for every policy a key control relies on, naming its owner, its audience and the controls it deploys.
Each row resolves to a published version whose approval record names the approver and the date decided.
Every approver holds authority over that policy's subject under the delegation schedule, and decided before the version reached its audience.
A control stating it is deployed through a policy resolves to a register row, not to a document a team holds privately.
Policies whose owner has left or changed role surface as exceptions carrying a date.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the policy register as at period end, giving owner, audience, status and current version for every policy.
Obtain the approval decision held against each current version, naming the requester, the approver and the date.
Obtain the delegation schedule showing who may approve a policy on each subject.
Export the policy-to-control links for the controls inside the reporting scope.
Obtain the staff roster and the leaver and mover lists covering the period.

Analysis:
Population is every policy in the register at period end. Test all of them for a named owner, a stated audience and a current version, since a sample cannot show an omission.
Sample 15 policies weighted towards those deploying key controls, and trace each to the decision held against the version now published.
Set each approver against the delegation schedule and judge whether that subject was theirs to approve.
Compare the decision date against the date the version was released to its audience.
Match every named owner to the roster, and to the leaver and mover lists.

Output:
A register exception list naming policies without an owner, an audience or an approved current version.
A sample result stating, per policy tested, the approver, the authority relied on and the days between decision and release.
A list of in-scope controls whose stated policy resolves to no register row.

title.en: Trace each key control to the policy that carries it

description.en: Walk from the control register into the policy library so the framework's boundary is drawn from the controls that depend on it, rather than from whichever documents happen to exist.

text.en: Pull the key controls in the reporting scope and note which of them name a policy behind them.
Open the policy library and match each named policy to a real record, marking those that resolve to nothing.
Add a row for any policy staff already follow that the library does not yet hold.
Mark the controls whose policy sits outside the library, such as a team wiki page or a shared drive.
Agree the resulting policy set with the control owners before ownership is assigned.

title.en: Assign each policy to a named owner and a defined audience

description.en: Give every policy record an accountable individual and the population it binds, using the fields the policy module already carries rather than a spreadsheet kept beside it.

text.en: Name one individual as owner on each policy record, not a team mailbox or a job family.
State the audience the policy binds, separating employees, contractors and third parties where they differ.
Link each policy to the controls it deploys so the dependency is navigable from either side.
Set the review frequency on the record so the next review date is computed rather than remembered.
Note the approval authority the subject demands, taken from the delegation schedule.

title.en: Put each new or changed policy through approval before it is issued

description.en: Publish the text as a version, obtain a recorded decision against that version, and release it to the audience only afterwards, so nobody is bound by a document nobody approved.

evidenceHint.en: The published version record and the decision held against it, naming who approved, on what date, and which version number was then released to the audience.

text.en: Publish the drafted text as a new policy version carrying a change summary against the version it replaces.
Raise the approval request against that version and route it to the authority the subject demands.
Capture the approver's decision, date and comment on the version itself, not in an email thread.
Release the version to its audience only once the decision is recorded as approved.
Retire the superseded version so the library returns only the text now in force.

title.en: Reconcile the register's named owners to the current roster

description.en: Test the ownership half of the framework by putting every named owner against the staff roster and the leaver list, since an owner who has left is the ordinary way a policy goes stale.

text.en: Export the register with the owner named against each policy as at the review date.
Match each owner to the roster, and to the leaver and mover lists for the period.
Raise an exception for every policy whose owner has left, moved on or cannot be identified.
Reassign each exception to a successor and record the date the handover took effect.
Report the count of unowned policies beside the size of the register that produced it.

templates.title: Policies distributed and attestation obtained
templates.description: The route by which a policy reaches the people it binds, with each person's attestation recorded against the specific version they were asked to follow.
templates.objective: To ensure each policy in force reaches everyone it binds and that their attestation is recorded against the exact version they were asked to follow, not the policy in general.
templates.successCriteria:
Every policy in force defines its audience by a rule the roster can be run against, rather than by a list typed once.
Each person the rule returns holds an assignment naming the version currently in force.
Attestations recorded in the period resolve to a person on the roster and to a version published on or before the date given.
Outstanding items are readable per policy with an age, and those past the deadline carry a dated referral.
A republished version that changes an obligation raises fresh assignments instead of inheriting the previous receipts.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export, per policy in force, the audience rule and the assignment list generated from it.
Export the attestation records for the period, each naming the person, the version and the timestamp.
Obtain the staff roster with joiner and mover dates covering the period.
Obtain the outstanding report and the referrals raised on items past their deadline.
Obtain the version history for the policies republished during the period.

Analysis:
Population is every person the audience rules return at period end. Reconcile the assignment lists against that population in full, because an omitted person appears in no sample of those who responded.
Sample 25 attestations spread across at least five policies and weighted to those deploying key controls, and confirm each names the version in force on the date attested.
Take the period's joiners and movers as a second population and test whether an assignment was raised within the stated window of their entering the audience.
Age each open item against its deadline and match it to a referral.
For each republished version, determine whether prior receipts were carried over or fresh assignments raised.

Output:
A per-policy completion rate stating the denominator used and the date it was drawn.
An exception list of people inside an audience holding no assignment, and of attestations naming a superseded version.
A findings note on joiners who performed a policy's duties before attesting to it.

title.en: Express each policy's audience as a rule over roles and units

description.en: Decide who a policy binds by a rule that can be run against the roster, so the audience re-derives itself as people join and move instead of ageing from the day it was typed.

text.en: State, per policy, the roles, units and contract types that fall inside its audience.
Run the rule against the current roster and read the population it returns.
Compare that population against who actually performs the controls the policy deploys.
Settle the treatment of contractors and secondees, who sit outside the employee roster.
Hold the rule against the policy record so the same rule produces the next campaign.

title.en: Bind the current version to everyone the audience rule returns

description.en: Create the acknowledgement assignments from the rule's output against the version in force, so the requirement is held per person and the outstanding list can be read off rather than reconstructed.

text.en: Raise an acknowledgement assignment for each person the rule returns, against the published version.
Set the deadline the assignment must be met by, and state where that deadline came from.
Check the assignment count against the population the rule returned and explain any difference.
Send the request through the policy module so the record and the notification cannot diverge.
Confirm each assignment names a version number rather than the policy alone.

title.en: Raise an assignment when a joiner or mover enters an audience

description.en: Catch the people who arrive between campaigns, since someone performing a control before attesting to the policy behind it is exactly the gap a period-end completion rate hides.

evidenceHint.en: The joiner and mover feed for the period set beside the assignment created for each one, showing the days between entering an audience and the requirement being raised.

text.en: Take the joiner and mover feed at the agreed interval and re-run each policy's audience rule.
Raise assignments for people who entered an audience since the rule last ran.
Withdraw assignments for people who left an audience, recording why they were withdrawn.
Hold a joiner to the onboarding deadline rather than waiting for the next campaign date.
Note any person who performed the policy's duties before their assignment existed.

title.en: Refer unanswered assignments to the manager once the deadline passes

description.en: Turn an outstanding list into a decision with a name against it, because an attestation campaign carrying no escalation arm closes every period at the same incomplete rate.

evidenceHint.en: The outstanding report per policy showing the age of each open item, with the referrals sent to line managers, the date each was raised and how it was resolved.

text.en: Read the outstanding list per policy and age each open item against its deadline.
Refer items past the deadline to the person's line manager, naming the policy and version.
Record the resolution of each referral, including a refusal and the reason given for it.
Escalate a refusal on a policy deploying a key control to that control's owner.
Close the campaign with a stated count of items never answered.

title.en: Recompute the completion rate on a freshly drawn audience

description.en: Re-derive the denominator at the review date and recompute the rate against it, since a figure quoted on the population captured when the campaign opened flatters itself.

text.en: Re-run each audience rule at the review date and take the population it returns now.
Recompute the rate against that population rather than the campaign's original list.
Test a sample of recorded attestations back to the version in force on the date given.
Identify attestations recorded against a version that had already been superseded.
Report both rates side by side with the date each denominator was drawn.

templates.title: Policies reviewed and reapproved on a defined cycle
templates.description: The periodic re-examination of each policy at an interval set for its subject, with the reviewer's conclusion recorded and a fresh approval obtained wherever the text moved.
templates.objective: To ensure every policy is re-examined at the interval its subject warrants, with the reviewer's conclusion recorded even where the text was left unchanged and re-approved where it moved.
templates.successCriteria:
Every policy carries a review interval and a next-review date computed from it, not an interval asserted in the text alone.
Each review in the period names its reviewer, the date decided and the conclusion, including a conclusion of no change.
A review that altered an obligation produced a new version with its own approval, not an edit to the version already in force.
Policies past their next-review date appear on a due list with the days elapsed and a dated owner action against each.
Intervals differ across the register in a way the subjects explain, rather than every policy sitting on twelve months.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Export the register showing review interval, last-reviewed date and next-review date for every policy in force.
Obtain the review records completed in the period, each naming reviewer, date and conclusion.
Obtain the version history for the policies whose review concluded that a change was needed.
Obtain the approval decisions held against those new versions.
Obtain the overdue report as at period end and the actions recorded against each row.

Analysis:
Population is every policy in force at period end. Recompute last-reviewed plus interval across all of them and identify rows whose stored due date does not follow.
Sample 12 reviews from the period, weighted towards the policies deploying key controls, and confirm each carries a conclusion rather than only a date.
For every review concluding a change, trace through to the new version and confirm its approval post-dates the review.
Age each overdue row at period end and determine whether the recorded action pre-dates or follows the due date.
Set the intervals against the subjects they cover and challenge a uniform interval applied with no reasoning behind it.

Output:
A due-and-overdue schedule as at period end giving the days elapsed per policy.
A sample result stating reviewer, conclusion and, where the text moved, the version and approval that followed.
An exception list of stored due dates that do not follow from the interval and last review recorded.

title.en: Set the review interval each policy's subject warrants

description.en: Decide how often a policy has to be looked at from how fast its subject moves, instead of putting the whole register on one twelve-month cycle nobody chose deliberately.

text.en: Group the register by subject and note how often the rules under each subject move.
Give a shorter interval to policies whose process, system or regulation changes inside a year.
State the reasoning behind each interval so a reviewer can challenge it later.
Agree the intervals with the policy owners who will have to meet them.

title.en: Stamp the interval and next-review date onto every policy record

description.en: Put the agreed interval into the field that drives the due date, so the schedule computes itself from the last completed review rather than living in somebody's calendar.

text.en: Record the review frequency in days on each policy record, matching the agreed interval.
Set the last-reviewed date from evidence of the most recent completed review.
Confirm the due date the record computes matches the interval agreed for that policy.
Correct records whose stored due date does not follow from the interval and last review.
Draw the coming year's due schedule from the register itself, not from a separate tracker.

title.en: Conclude each policy falling due, including where nothing changed

description.en: Work the quarter's due list to a recorded judgement per policy, because a review nobody wrote down is indistinguishable afterwards from a review that never happened at all.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's due list with the review held against each policy on it, giving the reviewer, the date decided, the conclusion reached and the version raised where one followed.

text.en: Draw the policies whose next-review date falls inside the quarter.
Read each against the process it now describes and the controls it deploys.
Record the conclusion, the reviewer and the date even where the text is left alone.
Stamp the reviewed date so the next due date recomputes from this review.
Refer a policy the owner cannot reach inside the quarter to the register's owner.

title.en: Publish and re-approve the text a review found must change

description.en: Carry a review that found a change through the same route a new policy takes, so the audience attests to the text they must now follow rather than to the one it replaced.

evidenceHint.en: The new version with its change summary, the approval decision recorded against that version, and the assignments raised for its audience after publication.

text.en: Publish the revised text as a new version whose change summary names what moved.
Obtain approval against the new version rather than amending the one already approved.
Raise fresh acknowledgement assignments wherever the change alters what someone must do.
Leave the prior version's receipts attached to the version they were given for.
Tell the owners of the controls the policy deploys that the text underneath them moved.

title.en: Challenge intervals that outlast the subjects they were set for

description.en: Look back across the year at whether the cycle is calibrated: a policy amended between two scheduled reviews was on too long an interval, and one concluding no change every time may be on too short one.

text.en: Compare each policy's interval against the number of times its text moved in the year.
Shorten the interval on policies amended between two scheduled reviews.
Question an interval that has not moved since the register was first built.
Age the overdue rows at year end and report the days elapsed against each policy.
Put the revised intervals to the approver who set the original cycle.

templates.title: Inventory of ICFR-relevant service organizations
templates.description: Providers whose processing reaches a financial statement account are identified, held on the vendor register with the process and accounts they touch, and kept complete as services are taken on and dropped.
templates.objective: To ensure every service organization whose processing reaches a financial statement account sits on the vendor register with the process it serves and the assurance relied on recorded on it.
templates.successCriteria:
Every provider that processes, hosts or reports transactions reaching a financial statement account holds a vendor record naming the process and accounts it touches.
Each in-scope vendor record carries a criticality tier, a named business owner and the assurance route relied on.
The register reconciles to the payables population and the application inventory, and additions arising are dated.
A provider taken out of ICFR scope carries a written basis on its record rather than an implied one.
Sub-service organizations behind a registered provider are carried on the register in their own right.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the vendor register exported at period end, filtered to the records flagged ICFR-relevant - the population this control is tested against.
Collect the accounts payable ledger for the period and the application inventory, the two sources an unregistered provider is found from.
Retrieve the criticality tier, business owner and assurance route recorded on each in-scope record.
Gather the scoping notes for providers assessed and left out of ICFR scope during the period.
Obtain the contracts and service descriptions naming sub-service organizations behind registered providers.

Analysis:
Reconcile the payables ledger in full against the register, isolating every supplier paid for a service that touches a ledger balance.
Sample twelve in-scope records across the criticality tiers and test whether the process and accounts named on each match the service actually received.
Re-perform the relevance judgement on every exclusion recorded in the period rather than on a sample, since each one removes a provider from oversight entirely.
Trace the sub-service organizations named in sampled contracts through to a register entry of their own.
Compare the register against the prior period to find providers that left it with no basis recorded.

Output:
Reconciliation of payables and the application inventory to the register, naming every provider found on neither.
Schedule of the sampled records showing process, accounts, tier, owner and assurance route, with the fields left blank.
Statement of whether each exclusion carries a basis, and which were re-performed to a different conclusion.
List of sub-service organizations relied on but absent from the register.

title.en: Delimit which outsourced services reach a reported balance

description.en: Decide process by process which providers can move a financial statement account and which merely supply the business, so the register is scoped by exposure rather than by spend.

text.en: Name every process outsourced in whole or in part, from payroll and billing to custody and hosting.
Trace each outsourced process through to the accounts and assertions it can move.
Set the test that separates an ICFR-relevant provider from one touching no reported balance.
Record the relevance decision and its basis on each vendor record, exclusions included.

title.en: Populate the register from payables, payroll and the application inventory

description.en: Build the first complete population from the sources that show money leaving and finance data moving, rather than from the list procurement happens to hold.

text.en: Pull the supplier population from the accounts payable ledger for the whole period.
Add the hosted applications through which finance data is processed, stored or reported.
Open a vendor record for each provider that has none, naming its business owner.
Tag each record with a criticality tier and the assurance route that tier demands.

title.en: Register a new provider before it processes its first transaction

description.en: Catch the provider at onboarding, while the contract and the service description are in hand, instead of at the year-end scoping exercise when nobody recalls what was agreed.

evidenceHint.en: The quarter's register additions, each showing the date its record was opened against the date the service went live.

text.en: Take the quarter's executed contracts and new suppliers as the arrival list.
Open the vendor record with process, accounts, owner and tier before go-live.
Attach the contract and service description to the record as vendor documents.
Escalate any provider already processing without a record to the control owner.

title.en: Reconcile the register to what the ledger actually paid for

description.en: Test completeness from outside the register: start from the payments made and the access granted, then see which providers the register never heard of.

text.en: Compare the payables population against the register and list what appears on neither.
Challenge exclusions where the service description contradicts the stated basis.
Check that sub-service organizations named in reports hold records of their own.
Refer unresolved gaps to the control owner with a date for closure.

templates.title: SOC 1 or equivalent reports obtained and reviewed
templates.description: An attestation report covering each relied-upon service is obtained for the whole reporting period, attached to the vendor record, and read against what the organization actually relies on.
templates.objective: To ensure an attestation report covering each provider's relied-upon services and the whole reporting period is obtained, read against that reliance, and concluded on in writing.
templates.successCriteria:
Each provider whose tier demands assurance has a current report on its vendor record, the period covered held in its validity dates.
The report's scope covers the services actually relied on, and any service outside that scope is named.
A dated review note per report records the opinion type, the deviations disclosed and the conclusion for reporting.
The gap between the report period end and the year end is covered by a bridge letter or by procedures performed here.
Sub-service organizations carved out of a report are identified, and assurance over each is obtained or its absence accepted.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of in-scope providers whose criticality tier demands an attestation report - the population, from which every critical provider and a sample of eight others are tested.
Collect the reports attached to those vendor records, with the validity dates recorded against each document.
Retrieve the dated review note behind each report and the bridge letter covering the gap period.
Gather the service descriptions or contracts stating what each provider actually performs.
Obtain the register of sub-service organizations carved out of the reports collected.

Analysis:
Compare each report's period against the organization's financial year and measure the uncovered days.
Set the scope section of each sampled report against the service description to find reliance the report never examined.
Read every disclosed testing deviation in the sampled reports and check it appears in the review note rather than only in the report.
Confirm the review note carries a date, an author and a conclusion expressed for financial reporting, not a filing stamp.
For carved-out sub-service organizations, trace through to a second report or to a recorded acceptance of the gap.

Output:
Schedule of the population showing report held, period covered, uncovered days and bridge letter status.
List of relied-upon services falling outside the scope of the report obtained for them.
Statement of which sampled reports carry a review note and which were filed unread.
List of carved-out sub-service organizations with no assurance and no recorded acceptance.

title.en: Determine which providers owe a report and what would satisfy it

description.en: Fix the assurance expectation per provider before the reporting season: which need a type 2 attestation, which are met by other evidence, and which the organization will test for itself.

text.en: Take the ICFR-relevant vendor records as the population that owes assurance.
State per criticality tier what report or alternative evidence will be accepted.
Name the services relied on that the report has to cover for each provider.
Record the accepted alternative where no attestation report exists at all.

title.en: Schedule each request against the provider's own reporting period

description.en: Turn that expectation into dates: when each report is published, when it is chased, and how the gap to the organization's year end will be covered.

text.en: Record each provider's report period end and its usual publication date.
Set the request and chase dates against the close calendar for the year.
Name the vendor contact the request will be sent to for each provider.
Decide per provider whether a bridge letter is needed for the gap period.

title.en: Attach the arriving report to its vendor record with the period it covers

description.en: File the report where the oversight actually lives, so its coverage period is visible on the record instead of buried in somebody's mailbox.

evidenceHint.en: The report filed as a vendor document, its validity dates set to the coverage period, with the bridge letter beside it.

text.en: Load the report against its vendor record as an attestation document.
Set the document validity dates to the period the report covers.
Attach the bridge letter covering the gap to the organization's year end.
Chase a provider whose report has not arrived by its scheduled date.

title.en: Examine the report against the services actually relied on

description.en: Do the reading this control exists to force: a report on file proves only that somebody asked for it, and an unread qualification is the same as no report at all.

evidenceHint.en: The dated review note per report, recording opinion type, scope match, disclosed deviations and the conclusion for financial reporting.

text.en: Compare the services described in the report against those the process relies on.
Record the opinion type and read the auditor's testing deviations in full.
Identify sub-service organizations carved out and what assurance covers them.
Write the conclusion for financial reporting, naming what it does not cover.

title.en: Challenge reports filed with no reader and no conclusion

description.en: Look for the failure the control exists to catch - a report collected, filed and never read - and for conclusions that stop short of naming an effect on the accounts.

text.en: Select the period's reports and look for a dated review note behind each.
Test whether a report's coverage period leaves the year end uncovered.
Judge whether the conclusion addresses the services the process actually uses.
Raise unread reports with the control owner and set a date for reading them.

templates.title: Complementary user entity controls identified and tested
templates.description: The controls an attestation report assumes the organization performs are extracted from the report, matched to a named internal control and owner, and tested for operating effectiveness over the report's own period.
templates.objective: To ensure the controls a service auditor's report assumes the organization performs are owned internally and tested for operating effectiveness, not merely listed and filed.
templates.successCriteria:
Every complementary user entity control stated in a relied-upon report is extracted into a list, cited to the section it came from.
Each extracted item is matched to a named internal control, its owner and its frequency, or recorded as having nothing behind it.
Operating effectiveness is tested over a sample drawn from the report's coverage period, with the sample size and basis recorded.
An item that fails its test or has nothing behind it is opened as a deficiency with an owner and a due date.
The extracted list is redrawn when a new report is issued or the way the service is consumed changes.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the extracted list of complementary user entity controls for every report relied on in the period - the population this control is tested against.
Collect the reports themselves, so the extraction can be checked back to the section it claims to come from.
Retrieve the mapping of each extracted item to an internal control, with owner and frequency.
Gather the test sheets: population, sample selected, items tested, exceptions and conclusion.
Obtain the deficiency entries opened for unowned items and failed tests, with their due dates.

Analysis:
Re-extract the user entity control section of three reports in full and compare against the list, since an omission here is invisible downstream.
Trace every extracted item to a mapped control and treat an unmapped item as a gap rather than as pending.
For eight mapped controls spanning at least three providers, re-perform two sample items each and compare the conclusion reached.
Check each sample was drawn from the report's coverage period rather than from the weeks before testing.
Compare the deficiency log against the failed and unowned items to find failures that never became deficiencies.

Output:
Schedule of extracted items per report showing mapped control, owner, frequency and test conclusion.
List of assumed controls with nothing behind them, and how long each has stood unowned.
Re-performance results for the eight controls tested, naming any conclusion not supported by the evidence.
Statement of whether the sample periods align to the reports, with the exceptions listed.

title.en: Extract the user entity controls each report assumes of us

description.en: Pull the assumptions out of the report and into a list that can be owned, citing each back to the section it came from so a reader can check rather than trust it.

text.en: Work through each report's user entity control section and list every assumption stated.
Cite each extracted item to the report, its version and the section it sits in.
Discard assumptions covering services this organization does not rely on.
Carry the surviving list onto the vendor record of the provider concerned.

title.en: Match each assumed control to an owner and a control that operates here

description.en: Turn an assumption into something testable: a named internal control, the individual who operates it and how often it runs, or an explicit statement that nothing behind it exists.

text.en: Map each assumption to a control in the register that already performs it.
Name the individual who operates that control and the frequency it runs at.
Mark assumptions with nothing behind them as gaps rather than as covered.
Agree the test approach and the sample basis for each matched control.

title.en: Test a sample drawn from the report's own coverage period

description.en: Do the part most often skipped: obtain evidence that the assumed control operated, across the period the service auditor relied on it operating.

evidenceHint.en: The test sheet per assumed control: population, sample selected, dates tested, exceptions found and the effectiveness conclusion.

text.en: Draw the population for each matched control over the period the report covers.
Select the sample on a stated basis and record why that size is sufficient.
Examine each item and record the exceptions rather than a pass rate alone.
Conclude in writing on whether the assumed control operated effectively.

title.en: Raise every unowned or failed assumption as a deficiency

description.en: Close the loop that identification leaves open, so an assumption nobody performs becomes a tracked deficiency with a date instead of another line in a list.

evidenceHint.en: The deficiency entries opened this cycle, each naming the assumption behind it, a remediation owner and a due date.

text.en: Open a deficiency for each assumption with no control or a failed test.
Assess the accounts and assertions that failure leaves exposed to misstatement.
Assign a remediation owner and a due date proportionate to that exposure.
Report the open items in the period's control reporting to the committee.

title.en: Judge whether the assumption list still fits the service taken

description.en: Re-read the list against how the service is consumed now, since a changed configuration can retire an assumption or introduce one nobody has extracted yet.

text.en: Compare this year's report section against the list drawn from last year's.
Identify changes in how the service is consumed since the list was drawn.
Retire assumptions that no longer apply, recording why each was dropped.
Add assumptions the current report states that the list never carried.

templates.title: Service organization report exceptions remediated
templates.description: Deviations, qualifications and failed user entity controls disclosed by a service organization's report are graded for their effect on the accounts, taken back to the provider with a date, and covered here until they close.
templates.objective: To ensure a deviation disclosed by a service organization's report is graded for its effect on the accounts, pursued to a dated fix, and covered by a procedure here while it stands.
templates.successCriteria:
Every deviation, qualification and exception disclosed by a report relied on is recorded and graded against the accounts it can misstate.
A graded deviation is put to the provider in writing and carries a remediation owner and a completion date.
Where reliance continues, a compensating procedure is performed here for each period the deviation remains open, and its output is kept.
Exceptions still open at the year-end conclusion are taken to management and the audit committee with their exposure stated.
Closure is evidenced by the following period's report rather than by the provider's own confirmation.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the exception schedule for the period - every deviation, qualification and failed user entity control disclosed by the reports relied on, which is the population tested.
Collect the reports themselves, so the schedule can be checked for omissions against what was disclosed.
Retrieve the correspondence putting each graded deviation to the provider, with the remediation plan returned.
Gather the compensating procedures performed while exceptions stood open, with their dated output.
Obtain the papers taken to management and the audit committee, and the following period's reports.

Analysis:
Re-read the deviations section of every report in full against the schedule, as an omitted exception is the failure with no downstream trace.
Sample six graded deviations across providers and test whether the grading follows the materiality thresholds set for the period.
For each sampled item still open, confirm the compensating procedure was performed in every period it was required, not only the first.
Compare the closure dates claimed with the results in the following period's report and note deviations that repeat.
Trace items open at year end into the committee papers and into the conclusion reached on internal control.

Output:
Reconciliation of report disclosures to the exception schedule, naming what never reached it.
Grading results for the six sampled deviations, with those graded below the threshold the accounts suggest.
Schedule of compensating procedures due and performed per open exception, with the periods missed.
List of deviations repeating in the following report despite a recorded closure.

title.en: Grade each disclosed deviation by the account it can misstate

description.en: Separate the deviations that reach the financial statements from those that do not, so effort follows exposure rather than the order in which the report happened to list them.

text.en: Collect every exception, qualification and deviation the period's reports disclosed.
Trace each one through to the service relied on and the accounts behind it.
Rate the exposure against the materiality thresholds already set for the period.
Discard deviations touching services this organization does not consume.

title.en: Agree a dated fix with the provider through its contract owner

description.en: Take the exception back to the provider through the relationship that can actually move it, and come away with a date rather than an assurance that it is being looked at.

text.en: Put the graded exceptions to the provider's named contact in writing.
Obtain a remediation plan carrying an owner and a completion date.
Record the plan against the vendor record as a document, not in an inbox.
Escalate to the contract owner where no date is offered at all.

title.en: Run the compensating procedure for as long as the exception stands

description.en: Cover the exposure here while the provider's fix is outstanding, because reliance on the service carries on whether or not the deviation has been closed.

evidenceHint.en: The completed procedure for every period it was required, showing the items checked, the differences found and who performed it.

text.en: Design a procedure that detects what the failed provider control would have caught.
Perform it in each period the exception remains open and keep the output.
Record the differences found and follow every one to a resolution.
Stop the procedure only once the provider's fix has been evidenced.

title.en: Table unresolved exceptions before the year-end conclusion

description.en: Put the open items in front of the people who sign the assessment while there is still time to do something other than disclose them.

evidenceHint.en: The schedule taken to management and the audit committee, showing status, exposure and the procedure standing behind each open item.

text.en: Compile the open exceptions with exposure, owner and expected closure date.
State for each what compensating procedure is standing in the meantime.
Take the schedule to management and to the audit committee in session.
Minute the decisions reached on items that will not close before sign-off.

title.en: Verify the next report shows the deviation closed

description.en: Test the provider's claim against the only independent evidence there is, the following period's attestation, instead of against its own confirmation email.

text.en: Take the prior period's exception list into the new report's testing results.
Confirm each closed item is absent from the current period's deviations.
Reopen any exception the new report repeats, with the history attached.
Report repeat deviations as a provider performance matter, not a new finding.

templates.title: Code of conduct approved by the board and published
templates.description: The standards of conduct the organization holds itself to, approved at board level and made available to everyone bound by them.
templates.objective: To ensure the conduct standards the organization expects are fixed by a board-level decision and published to everyone bound by them, rather than asserted informally.
templates.successCriteria:
A current code of conduct exists with a recorded board or equivalent approval naming the version and the date it was agreed.
The published version matches the approved version exactly, with no undated or draft copy reachable to a reader.
Every population bound by the code has a route to the current version, including contractors, agency staff and directors.
A review cycle is defined, the last review fell within it, and the reviewer and outcome are recorded even where nothing changed.
Superseded versions are withdrawn from every location a reader could still reach them from.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current code of conduct and the minute or resolution recording its approval.
Obtain the publication location and the date the approved version was posted there.
Collect the distribution list or access route for each population bound by the code, including contractors.
Obtain the defined review cycle and the record of the most recent review.
Request any superseded versions still reachable to staff.

Analysis:
Compare the published document against the approved version to confirm they are the same text.
Set the approval date against the publication date to confirm publication followed approval.
Test whether each bound population has a route to the current version, not only permanent employees.
Compare the last review date against the stated cycle and judge whether the cycle has lapsed.
Inspect the publication location for superseded copies that a reader could mistake for current.

Output:
Record whether a current, approved and published code exists, naming its approval date and reviewer.
List any population bound by the code without a route to it.
State whether the review cycle is being met, and by how far it has lapsed if not.

title.en: Establish the conduct standards the organization will hold

description.en: Draft or confirm the code's content, covering the conduct areas the organization's activities actually expose it to rather than a generic template.

text.en: List the conduct areas the organization's operations expose it to, such as conflicts of interest, gifts, confidentiality and fair dealing.
Identify every population the code will bind, separating employees, contractors, temporary workers and directors.
Draft the code text against those areas, stating expected behaviour rather than aspirations.
Record which existing policies the code defers to, so an obligation is stated once rather than in several places.

title.en: Obtain board approval and record the decision

description.en: Take the code to the board or equivalent body and capture the approval as a dated record, since an unapproved code carries no authority.

text.en: Table the drafted code at the board or committee holding the approval authority.
Capture the approval in the minute, naming the version approved and the date it was agreed.
Record any changes the board required and confirm they are carried into the approved version.
File the approved version so the minute and the document can be tied together later.

title.en: Publish the approved code to every bound population

description.en: Put the approved version where each bound population can reach it, and remove earlier copies that could be mistaken for current.

evidenceHint.en: The publication location showing the approved version and its posting date, with the distribution route recorded for each bound population.

text.en: Publish the approved version to the intranet or handbook location staff are directed to.
Provide a route for contractors and temporary workers who do not have intranet access.
Withdraw superseded versions from every location where a reader could still reach them.
Record the posting date so publication can be shown to have followed approval.

title.en: Review the code against the defined cycle

description.en: Re-examine the code on its stated cycle and record the outcome, so a code nobody has revisited becomes visible as such.

text.en: Compare the last review date against the stated cycle and open the review when it falls due.
Assess whether the conduct areas covered still match the organization's activities and exposures.
Record the review outcome, including a decision that no change was needed, with the reviewer named.
Return the code for re-approval where the review changed its substance.

templates.title: Annual code of conduct acknowledgement obtained
templates.description: A yearly confirmation from every person bound by the code that they have read the version in force and accept the obligations it places on them.
templates.objective: To ensure every person bound by the code confirms each year that they have read the version in force and accept the obligations it places on them.
templates.successCriteria:
The population bound for the cycle is drawn from named source systems at a stated as-of date, with contractors and directors included.
Every receipt is attributable to a named individual, carries a date, and cites the version of the code in force.
Names still outstanding at the close of the cycle are listed with the escalation taken against each.
People joining after the cycle closed acknowledged the code inside the onboarding window set for them.
Refusals and qualified responses are held separately and routed to a named owner rather than counted as complete.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the acknowledgement register for the cycle as exported at the date of test.
Obtain the HR master list, the contractor and agency rosters and the director list as at the cycle's as-of date.
Collect the acknowledgement wording issued and the code version it referred to.
Obtain the reminder and escalation correspondence covering the outstanding population.
Collect the list of people who started after the cycle closed, with each start date.

Analysis:
Reconcile the register against the combined population sources and quantify people bound but never issued a request.
Sample 25 receipts spread across employees, contractors and directors, and test each for attribution, date and the code version cited.
Trace every name outstanding at close to the escalation taken, and judge whether it ended in a receipt, a refusal or nothing.
Test the whole joiner population against the onboarding window, measuring days from start date to receipt.
Inspect refusals and qualified responses for routing to a named owner rather than closure as complete.

Output:
Completion figure for the cycle expressed as receipts over the bound population, with the denominator named.
Schedule of people bound by the code holding no receipt, split by employee, contractor and director.
Exception list of receipts that are undated, unattributable or cite a superseded version of the code.
Statement of joiner timeliness naming those outside the window and by how many days.

title.en: Draw the population bound by the code for this cycle

description.en: Fix who must acknowledge this year from named source systems, and set the as-of date the population is measured at, so a completeness figure later has a denominator that can be defended.

text.en: Export the employee list from the HR system as at the cycle's as-of date, including people on leave.
Add contractors, agency and temporary workers from the procurement and agency rosters, which HR master data does not carry.
Add directors and officers, who are bound by the code but sit outside payroll reporting.
State the cut-off date after which a new starter is handled by the joiner route instead of this cycle.
Note any exclusion from the population with the reason for it and the person who approved it.

title.en: Prepare the acknowledgement statement and its issue route

description.en: Settle the words a person is agreeing to, tie them to the version of the code in force, and decide how the request reaches populations without a corporate mailbox.

text.en: Draft the statement so it covers reading the code, accepting its obligations and the duty to report a breach.
Bind the statement to the code version and date in force, so a later receipt shows what was accepted.
Configure the capture so each response carries the person's identity and a timestamp that cannot be edited.
Agree a paper or supervised route for contractors and site staff who hold no corporate mailbox.
Set the response window, the reminder dates and the point at which a name is escalated.

title.en: Collect receipts across the cycle and clear what is outstanding

description.en: Issue the request to the drawn population, work the reminder and escalation schedule, and bring every name to a receipt, a refusal or a recorded escalation.

evidenceHint.en: The acknowledgement register for the cycle showing each person, the date received and the code version accepted, alongside the closing list of names still unresolved.

text.en: Issue the request to every name in the drawn population and log the issue date against each.
Send reminders on the agreed dates and refresh the outstanding list after each pass.
Escalate names still outstanding at the end of the window to their line manager and capture the response.
Separate refusals and qualified responses, and route each to the named owner for handling.
Close the cycle with a dated completion figure stated over the population drawn at the start.

title.en: Capture joiner acknowledgements inside the onboarding window

description.en: Take the acknowledgement from people who join after the cycle has closed, as part of onboarding, rather than leaving them unbound until the next annual pass.

evidenceHint.en: The onboarding or induction record for each starter in the period, carrying the date the code was acknowledged set against that person's start date.

text.en: Place the acknowledgement step in the onboarding checklist so it falls in the joiner's first week.
Take the receipt against the code version in force on the joiner's start date.
Compare new starters against receipts each month to find joiners the onboarding route missed.
Escalate any joiner past the onboarding window to the hiring manager and note the outcome.
Feed joiner receipts into the register the annual cycle writes to, so one population view exists.

title.en: Reconcile receipts to the bound population and report the gap

description.en: Set the receipts collected against the population that was bound, quantify the shortfall by category, and put the result in front of the owner accountable for the code.

text.en: Match the register to the population source used at the start of the cycle, name by name.
Quantify people bound but never issued a request, apart from those issued and not responding.
Split the shortfall by employee, contractor and director, since each has a different route and owner.
Test a sample of receipts for attribution, date and the code version they cite.
Report the completion figure and the unresolved names to the code owner with a date for clearance.

templates.title: Code of conduct waivers and exceptions reviewed
templates.description: The record of departures from the code, showing who was permitted what, on whose authority and for how long, and the periodic examination of that record as a whole.
templates.objective: To ensure a departure from the code happens only with a stated reason, an approver holding the level set for that provision, and a fixed expiry, rather than by quiet practice.
templates.successCriteria:
Every departure granted in the period sits in one register, with the code provision it departs from named.
Each entry carries the requester, the business reason, the conditions attached and a firm expiry date.
The approver of each grant held the level set for that provision, and no grant was approved by the person it benefits.
Grants benefiting directors or executive officers were escalated to the audit committee or board, with the disclosure decision recorded.
Expired grants are closed or re-argued on their own record instead of running on unexamined.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the waiver register for the period, with the provision, approver, conditions and expiry on each entry.
Obtain the document setting which provisions admit a departure and the approval level reserved for each.
Collect the request and approval correspondence behind a sample of entries.
Obtain the audit committee or board papers covering grants to directors and executive officers.
Collect the gift, hospitality, outside-interest and related-party declarations logged in the period, as an independent source.

Analysis:
Trace declarations logged outside the register into it, to surface exceptions granted informally.
Sample 15 entries weighted towards senior grantees and test each approver against the level set for that provision.
Test whether any grant was approved by the person it benefits or by someone reporting to them.
Group the period's grants by provision, business unit and grantee, and judge whether a repeat signals a provision out of step with practice.
Compare expiry dates against current status to find grants still operating past their term.
Check each director and executive officer case against the escalation record and the disclosure decision taken.

Output:
Schedule of the period's grants by provision, naming the approver and their level against each.
List of exceptions found in the declarations but absent from the register.
Findings on self-approval, expired grants still running, and concentration by grantee or unit.
Statement of whether every senior case reached the audit committee, naming any that did not.

title.en: Define which code provisions admit a departure, and at what level

description.en: Separate the provisions where a documented exception is possible from those that admit none, and fix the approval level each requires before any request arrives.

text.en: Identify the code provisions where practice creates genuine exceptions, such as gifts, hospitality and outside interests.
Name the provisions that admit no exception at all, so a request against them is refused rather than negotiated.
Set the approval level per provision, reserving director and executive officer cases for the board or its committee.
Fix the fields every entry must carry, including the conditions attached and a firm expiry date.
State how long a grant may run before it has to be re-argued rather than rolled forward.

title.en: Open one register and pull informal approvals into it

description.en: Stand up a single record of departures from the code, and move approvals currently sitting in mailboxes and local files into it, so the period's population is complete.

text.en: Create the register with the agreed fields: requester, provision, reason, conditions, approver and expiry.
Search mailboxes and shared drives for approvals already given, and enter those still in force.
Publish the request route so a person seeking an exception lands in the register rather than an inbox.
Restrict who may edit a granted entry, and keep a trail of changes to its conditions or expiry.
Agree retention for closed entries, so a lapsed grant can still be examined after the fact.

title.en: Grant or refuse each request at the level set for it
